title.zh: 卷四百十四 列傳第一百七十三 史弥远 鄭清之 史嵩之 董槐 葉夢鼎 馬廷鸞
title.en: Volume 414 Biographies 173: Shi Miyuan, Zheng Qingzhi, Shi Songzhi, Dong Huai, Ye Mengding, Ma Tingluan
title.raw: 卷四百十四 列傳第一百七十三 史弥远 鄭清之 史嵩之 董槐 葉夢鼎 馬廷鸞 Volume 414 Biographies 173: Shi Miyuan, Zheng Qingzhi, Shi Songzhi, Dong Huai, Ye Mengding, Ma Tingluan

sentences.zh: 史彌遠 鄭清之 史嵩之 董槐 葉夢鼎 馬廷鸞

translations.literal: Shi Miyuan, Zheng Qingzhi, Shi Songzhi, Dong Huai, Ye Mengding, Ma Tingluan
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan, Zheng Qingzhi, Shi Songzhi, Dong Huai, Ye Mengding, and Ma Tingluan

sentences.zh: 史彌遠

translations.literal: Shi Miyuan
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan

sentences.zh: 史彌遠，字同叔，浩之子也。

translations.literal: Shi Miyuan, styled Tongshu, was a son of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan, whose style was Tongshu, was the son of Shi Hao.

sentences.zh: 淳熙六年，補承事郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chunxi, he was granted the rank of Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Chunxi era (1179), he received appointment as Gentleman for Attendance.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉宣義郎，銓試第一，調建康府糧料院，改沿海制置司幹辦公事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was promoted to Gentleman for Propagating Righteousness; he ranked first in the selection examination, was assigned to the Grain Supply Office of Jiankang Prefecture, and was transferred to serve as a staff officer of the Coastal Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was promoted to Gentleman for Propagating Righteousness, placed first in the civil-service examination, posted to the grain-supply office of Jiankang Prefecture, and then transferred to the Coastal Pacification Commission as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 十四年，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Chunxi he passed the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，授大理司直。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi, he was appointed Directing Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxi (1190) he was appointed Directing Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷太社令。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to be Director of the Altar of the God of the Soil.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Director of the Altar of the God of the Soil.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷太常寺主簿，以親老請祠，主管沖佑觀。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to be Registrar of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; citing his parents' advanced age, he requested a temple sinecure and was put in charge of Chongyou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Registrar of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; because his parents were elderly he asked for a temple appointment and was assigned to administer Chongyou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He then went into mourning upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 慶元二年，復為大理司直，尋改諸王宮大小學教授。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingyuan, he was again made Directing Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, and soon after was changed to Professor of the Greater and Lesser Schools of the Princes' Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qingyuan (1196) he returned to the post of Directing Clerk at the Court of Judicial Review, and shortly thereafter became professor at the Greater and Lesser Schools for imperial clansmen.

sentences.zh: 輪對，乞旌廉潔之士，推舉薦之賞；

translations.literal: At a rotating audience, he requested that incorrupt officials be honored and that rewards for recommendation and nomination be expanded;
translations.idiomatic: At a rotating audience with the throne he asked that men of integrity be publicly honored and that greater rewards be given for recommending them;

sentences.zh: 浚溝洫，固堤防，實倉廩，均賦役，課農桑，禁末作，為水旱之備；

translations.literal: that ditches and canals be dredged, dikes strengthened, granaries filled, tax and corvée burdens equalized, agriculture and sericulture encouraged, nonessential crafts restricted, and preparations made against flood and drought;
translations.idiomatic: that canals be dredged, dikes reinforced, granaries stocked, tax and labor levies made equitable, farming and silk production promoted, luxury trades curbed, and every measure taken to guard against flood and drought;

sentences.zh: 葺城郭，修器械，選將帥，練士卒，儲粟穀，明烽燧，為邊鄙之防。

translations.literal: that city walls be repaired, weapons maintained, generals selected, troops drilled, grain stored, beacon signals kept clear, and defenses for the frontier prepared.
translations.idiomatic: and that city walls be restored, arms readied, commanders chosen, soldiers trained, grain hoarded, beacon lines kept in order, and the frontier made secure against invasion.

sentences.zh: 丞相京鏜屏左右曰：「君他日功名事業過鏜遠甚，願以子孫為托。」

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Jing Yong dismissed those around him and said, "Sir, your future fame and achievements will far surpass mine; I entrust my descendants to you."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Jing Yong sent his attendants away and said, "Your future career will far outshine mine; I ask you to look after my children."

sentences.zh: 四年，授樞密院編修官，遷太常丞，尋兼工部郎官，改刑部。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, soon after concurrently made a Secretary in the Ministry of Works, and then transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qingyuan he was made a compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, soon given a concurrent post in the Ministry of Works, and then moved to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 六年，改宗正丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was transferred to be Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 丐外，知池州。

translations.literal: He begged an outside appointment and was made prefect of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a provincial post and was appointed prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰四年，提舉浙西常平。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiatai, he was made Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries for Western Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiatai (1204) he was appointed intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries in western Zhe.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年，授司封郎官兼國史編修、實錄檢討，遷秘書少監，遷起居郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaixi, he was appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Rites in charge of enfeoffments, concurrently Compiler of the National History and Reviser of the Veritable Records; he was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Library and then to Recorder of the Emperor's Actions.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaixi (1205) he became a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, with concurrent duties on the National History and Veritable Records, then rose to Vice Director of the Palace Library and Recorder of the Emperor's Actions.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼資善堂直講。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was concurrently made Lecturer at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaixi he also served as lecturer at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄建開邊之議，以堅寵固位，已而邊兵大衄，詔在位者言事，彌遠上疏曰：「今之議者，以為先發者制人，後發者制於人，此為將之事，施於一勝一負之間，則可以爭雄而捷出。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou proposed opening the frontier to war in order to secure favor and consolidate power; soon the border armies suffered great defeats. An edict called on those in office to speak out. Miyuan submitted a memorial saying: "Those who debate today hold that he who strikes first controls others, while he who strikes later is controlled by others. This is the business of generals, applicable when victory and defeat hang on a single contest, so that one may vie for supremacy and act swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou had urged war on the northern frontier to shore up his power; when the border armies were routed, the court ordered officials to speak freely. Miyuan memorialized: "Counselors today say that whoever strikes first controls the enemy and whoever delays is controlled. That may hold for generals in a single battle fought for immediate victory.

sentences.zh: 若夫事關國體、宗廟社稷，所系甚重，詎可舉數千萬人之命輕於一擲乎？

translations.literal: But when the matter concerns the body politic, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain—matters of the gravest weight—how can the lives of tens of millions be wagered lightly on a single throw?
translations.idiomatic: But when the fate of the dynasty, the ancestral shrines, and the realm itself is at stake, how can we stake the lives of millions on one gamble?

sentences.zh: 京師根本之地，今出戍既多，留衛者寡，萬一盜賊竊發，誰其禦之？

translations.literal: The capital is the root of the realm; with so many troops now sent out on campaign, those left to guard it are few. If bandits should rise in secret, who will repel them?
translations.idiomatic: The capital is the heart of the empire, yet so many troops have marched out that few remain to guard it. If thieves or rebels should strike, who will defend the city?

sentences.zh: 若夫沿江屯駐之兵，各當一面，皆所以拱護行都，尤當整備，繼今勿輕調發，則內外表裏俱有足恃，而無可伺之隙矣。

translations.literal: As for the garrison troops stationed along the Yangzi, each holding one sector—all exist to shield the traveling capital—they above all must be kept in readiness. From now on they must not be lightly redeployed; then within and without, inner and outer, will all have sufficient strength to rely on, and no gap for the enemy to exploit.
translations.idiomatic: The armies posted along the Yangzi, each guarding its sector, exist to protect the mobile capital and must be kept at full strength. They should not be redeployed lightly; then court and frontier alike will be secure, with no opening for the enemy to probe.

sentences.zh: 所遣撫諭之臣，止令按曆邊陲，招集逋寇，戒飭將士，固守封圻。

translations.literal: The commissioners sent to pacify and instruct should be ordered only to tour the borderlands, gather scattered bandits, admonish officers and soldiers, and hold fast to the frontier domains.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys sent to the borders should be told only to inspect the frontier, rally deserters and stragglers, warn the troops, and hold the line.

sentences.zh: 毋惑浮言以撓吾之規，毋貪小利以滋敵之釁，使民力愈寬，國勢愈壯，遲之歲月，以俟大舉，實宗社無疆之福。」

translations.literal: They must not be misled by loose talk that would upset our plans, nor grasp petty gains that would provoke the enemy. Let the people's strength grow ever more at ease and the state's power ever more robust; delay for months and years to await the great campaign—this will truly be boundless fortune for the altars of the dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: They must not heed reckless talk that would undo our strategy, nor chase small gains that would give the enemy cause to attack. Ease the burden on the people, strengthen the state, and wait months and years until we are ready for a major campaign. That will be the dynasty's lasting blessing."

sentences.zh: 奏方具，客曰：「侂胄必以奏議占人情，太夫人年高，能無貽親憂乎？」

translations.literal: As the memorial was just being completed, a guest said, "Tuozhou is sure to use your memorial to win popular sentiment. Your lady mother is advanced in years—can you avoid bringing worry upon her?"
translations.idiomatic: While he was finishing the memorial, someone warned him, "Tuozhou will use your words to court public favor. Your mother is elderly—will you not bring grief upon her?"

sentences.zh: 彌遠曰：「時事如此，言入而益于國，利於人，吾得罪甘心焉。」

translations.literal: Miyuan said, "The times are as they are. If my words enter the record and benefit the state and the people, I am content even to incur punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan replied, "These are desperate times. If what I say helps the realm and the people, I will accept punishment gladly."

sentences.zh: 封鄞縣男兼權刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Yin County and made Acting Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Yin County and appointed acting Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 三年，改禮部兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰，仍兼刑部。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites, concurrently made Associate Compiler of the National History and Associate Compiler of the Veritable Records, while still holding the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaixi he moved to the Ministry of Rites, with concurrent posts on the National History and Veritable Records, while retaining his Ministry of Justice duties.

sentences.zh: 兵端既開，敗衄相屬，累使求和，金人不聽。

translations.literal: Once hostilities had begun, defeats followed one after another. Envoys were repeatedly sent to sue for peace, but the Jurchens would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: After war broke out, defeat followed defeat. Repeated embassies sought peace, but the Jin court refused.

sentences.zh: 都城震搖，宮闈疑懼，常若禍在朝暮，然皆畏侂胄莫敢言。

translations.literal: The capital trembled; the palace was filled with dread, as though disaster might come at any dawn or dusk—yet all feared Tuozhou and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was shaken and the inner palace lived in fear, as if ruin might come any day, yet everyone was afraid of Tuozhou and kept silent.

sentences.zh: 彌遠力陳危迫之勢，皇子詢聞之，亟具奏，乃罷侂胄並陳自強右丞相。

translations.literal: Miyuan forcefully set forth the gravity of the crisis. The prince Xun heard of it and quickly submitted a memorial; Tuozhou was then dismissed and Chen Ziqiang was made Right Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan urgently described the peril facing the dynasty. Prince Xun heard him and at once memorialized the throne; Tuozhou was removed from office and Chen Ziqiang was appointed Right Chief Councillor.

sentences.zh: 既而台諫、給舍交章論駁，侂胄乃就誅。

translations.literal: Soon censors and remonstrators submitted memorial after memorial in rebuttal, and Tuozhou was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the censorate and remonstrance officials flooded the court with protests, and Tuozhou was executed.

sentences.zh: 召彌遠對延和殿，帝欲命為簽書樞密院事，力辭，乃遷禮部尚書兼國史實錄院修撰。

translations.literal: Miyuan was summoned to audience in the Yenhe Hall. The emperor wished to appoint him Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he firmly declined, and was instead promoted to Minister of Rites and Compiler of the National History and Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan was summoned to the Yenhe Hall. The emperor wanted to make him Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but he firmly declined and was promoted instead to Minister of Rites with duties on the National History and Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 詢立為太子，兼詹事，遣使詣金求和，金人以大散隔牙二關、濠州來歸，疏奏：「今兩淮、襄、漢沿邊之地，瘡痍未瘳，軍實未充。

translations.literal: Xun was established as crown prince, and Miyuan was made concurrently Grand Tutor. Envoys were sent to the Jin to sue for peace; the Jin returned the two passes of Dasan and Geya and Hao Prefecture. In a memorial he stated: "Today the borderlands along the two Huai, Xiang, and Han are still unhealed of their wounds, and military stores are not yet full.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was made crown prince, with Miyuan as his grand tutor. Envoys went to the Jin to negotiate peace; the Jin returned the passes of Dasan and Geya and Hao Prefecture. Miyuan memorialized: "The frontiers along the two Huai, the Xiang, and the Han are still devastated and our armies are not yet replenished.

sentences.zh: 當勉厲將帥，盡吾委寄之誠；

translations.literal: We should encourage and urge the generals to fulfill the trust placed in them;
translations.idiomatic: We must urge our commanders to honor the trust we place in them;

sentences.zh: 簡閱士卒，核其尺籍之闕。

translations.literal: inspect and review the soldiers and verify gaps in their muster rolls.
translations.idiomatic: inspect the troops and correct errors in the muster rolls.

sentences.zh: 繕城堡，葺器械，儲糗糧。

translations.literal: Repair fortresses and cities, restore weapons, and store provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Repair fortifications, restore arms, and stock provisions.

sentences.zh: 當聘使既通之後，常如干戈未定之日，推擇帥守以壯藩屏之勢，獎拔智勇以備緩急之求。」

translations.literal: After envoys have been exchanged, we should always act as though war were not yet settled: select commanders and prefects to strengthen the screen of the realm, and reward the wise and brave to meet sudden emergencies."
translations.idiomatic: Even after peace envoys have come and gone, we should live as though war were still unsettled: choose able governors and generals to strengthen our defenses, and promote the wise and brave for whatever crisis may come."

sentences.zh: 拜同知樞密院事兼太子賓客，進封伯。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince, and was advanced to the rank of earl.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince, and promoted to Earl.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年，遷知樞密院事，進奉化郡侯兼參知政事，拜右丞相兼樞密使兼太子少傅，進開國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading, he was transferred to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, advanced to Marquis of Fenghua Commandery and made Concurrent Administrator of Affairs, appointed Right Chief Councillor and Commissioner of Military Affairs and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, and advanced to Duke with the state of a founding meritocrat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiading (1208) he became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Marquis of Fenghua and Concurrent Administrator of Affairs, then Right Chief Councillor, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, and was raised to Duke of a founding meritocrat.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，歸治葬，太子請賜第行在，令就第持服，以便咨訪。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother, returned to arrange the burial, and the crown prince requested that a residence in the capital be granted so that he might observe mourning at home and remain available for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he went home to arrange the funeral. The crown prince asked that he be given a house in the capital so he could observe mourning there while remaining available for counsel.

sentences.zh: 二年，以使者趣行急，乃就道，起復右丞相兼樞密使兼太子少師。

translations.literal: In the second year, because envoys pressed him to hurry, he took the road and was recalled from mourning to resume the posts of Right Chief Councillor, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year envoys urged him to return in haste; he set out and was recalled from mourning to Right Chief Councillor, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 四年，落起復。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the notation of recall from mourning was removed from his record.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the stigma of being recalled from mourning was cleared from his record.

sentences.zh: 雪趙汝愚之冤，乞褒贈賜諡，厘正誣史，一時偽學党人朱熹、彭龜年、楊萬里、呂祖儉雖已歿，或褒贈易名，或錄用其後，召還正人故老於外。

translations.literal: He cleared the injustice done to Zhao Ruyu, requesting posthumous honors and an enfeoffment title, and corrected the slanderous histories. Men of the so-called False Learning faction of the time—Zhu Xi, Peng Guinian, Yang Wanli, and Lü Zuqian—though already dead, were either given posthumous honors and name changes or their descendants were employed; upright elders who had been in exile were summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: He vindicated Zhao Ruyu, sought posthumous honors and a title for him, and corrected the slander written into the histories. Zhu Xi, Peng Guinian, Yang Wanli, and Lü Zuqian of the banned "False Learning" faction, though dead, were posthumously honored or had their names restored; their descendants were given office, and worthy elders in exile were recalled.

sentences.zh: 十四年，賜家廟祭器。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was granted sacrificial vessels for his family temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Jiading he was granted ritual vessels for his ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 甯宗崩，擁立理宗，於是拜太師，依前右丞相兼樞密使，進封魏國公，六辭不拜，因乞解機政，歸田裏，亟出關，帝從之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong died, Miyuan installed Emperor Lizong. He was then appointed Grand Preceptor, retaining his former posts as Right Chief Councillor and Commissioner of Military Affairs, and was advanced to Duke of Wei. He declined six times and refused to accept; he then begged to be relieved of state affairs, to return to his fields, and hurried out of the pass—the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong died, Miyuan installed Lizong on the throne. He was made Grand Preceptor while keeping his posts as Right Chief Councillor and Commissioner of Military Affairs, and was raised to Duke of Wei. He declined six times, then asked to leave government, return to his estate, and quickly left the capital; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 實慶二年，拜少師，賜玉帶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoqing, he was appointed Junior Preceptor and granted a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoqing (1226) he was appointed Junior Preceptor and given a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 勸上傾心順承以事太后，力學修德以答皇天眷祐，以副四海歸戴。

translations.literal: He urged the emperor to devote his heart to obeying and serving the empress dowager, to study diligently and cultivate virtue in response to Heaven's favor, and to match the allegiance of all within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to serve the empress dowager wholeheartedly, study hard and cultivate virtue to repay Heaven's favor, and live up to the loyalty of the realm.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年，上太后尊號，拜太傅，八辭不拜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoding, when the empress dowager was given an honorific title, he was appointed Grand Tutor; he declined eight times and refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoding (1228), when the empress dowager received an honorific title, he was appointed Grand Tutor but declined eight times.

sentences.zh: 夏，得疾，累疏丐歸，不許。

translations.literal: In summer he fell ill and repeatedly memorialized begging to retire; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he fell ill and repeatedly asked to retire, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 都城災，五疏乞罷斥，乃降封奉化郡公。

translations.literal: When disaster struck the capital, he submitted five memorials begging to be dismissed; his enfeoffment was then reduced to Duke of Fenghua Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After a disaster in the capital he submitted five memorials asking to be removed from office, and his rank was reduced to Duke of Fenghua.

sentences.zh: 五年春，復爵。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, his title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year his original rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 六年，將拜太師，三具奏辭，乞免出命，不許。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when he was about to be appointed Grand Preceptor, he submitted three memorials declining and begged that the appointment not be issued; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when he was to be made Grand Preceptor, he declined three times and asked that the appointment be withheld, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 乃拜太師，依前右丞相兼樞密使、魯國公，又三具奏辭。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Grand Preceptor, retaining his former posts as Right Chief Councillor and Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Duke of Lu; he submitted three more memorials declining.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Grand Preceptor, remaining Right Chief Councillor and Commissioner of Military Affairs as Duke of Lu, and declined three more times.

sentences.zh: 紹定五年，上疏乞謝事，拜太傅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoding, he memorialized begging to resign from office and was appointed Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoding he asked to retire and was appointed Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜太師、左丞相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand Preceptor, Left Chief Councillor, and Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Grand Preceptor, Left Chief Councillor, and Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上疏乞解機政，依前太師特授保寧、昭信軍節度使，充醴泉觀使，進封會稽郡王。

translations.literal: He memorialized begging to be relieved of state affairs; retaining his rank as Grand Preceptor, he was specially appointed Military Commissioner of Baoning and Zhaoxin Armies and made Director of Liquan Abbey, and was advanced to Prince of Kuaiji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He asked again to leave government. He kept the title of Grand Preceptor but was given the nominal posts of Military Commissioner of Baoning and Zhaoxin and Director of Liquan Abbey, and was raised to Prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺表聞，帝震悼，輟朝三日，特贈中書令，追封衛王，諡忠獻。

translations.literal: He died. When his final memorial was received, the emperor was shaken with grief and suspended court for three days. He was specially posthumously appointed Director of the Secretariat, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, and given the posthumous title Zhongxian (Loyal and Offering).
translations.idiomatic: He died. When his deathbed memorial arrived, the emperor was stricken with grief and suspended court for three days. Miyuan was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, and given the posthumous title Loyal and Offering.

sentences.zh: 戶部支賻贈銀絹以千計，內帑特頒五千匹兩，遣使祭奠。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue disbursed condolence gifts of silver and silk numbering in the thousands; the inner treasury specially issued five thousand bolts and taels, and envoys were sent to offer sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue paid out thousands in silver and silk as funeral gifts; the inner treasury added five thousand bolts and taels, and envoys were sent to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 及其喪還，遣禮官致路祭於都門外，賜纛、佩玉、黝纁。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned, ritual officials were sent to perform roadside sacrifices outside the capital gate; he was granted a funeral banner, girdle pendants, and dark red and black vestments.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession returned, ritual officials offered sacrifices outside the city gate; he was granted a funeral banner, jade ornaments, and the dark red and black mourning robes.

sentences.zh: 初，誅李全，復淮安，克盱眙，第功行賞，諸將皆望不次拔擢。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li Quan was executed, Huai'an was recovered, and Xuyi was taken, rewards were graded by merit; the generals all hoped for extraordinary promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Li Quan was killed, Huai'an was recovered and Xuyi captured, and merit rewards were handed out; every general expected exceptional promotion.

sentences.zh: 或言於彌遠，彌遠曰：「禦將之道，譬如養鷹，饑則依入，飽則揚去。

translations.literal: Someone spoke to Miyuan about this. Miyuan said, "The way to control generals is like keeping a hawk: when hungry it comes to you; when full it flies away.
translations.idiomatic: When someone raised this with Miyuan, he said, "Commanding generals is like training a hawk: when it is hungry it stays with you; when it is full it flies off.

sentences.zh: 曹彬下江南，太祖未肯以使相與之。

translations.literal: When Cao Bin conquered the south, Taizu would not grant him the rank of commissioner or chief councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Bin conquered the south, Emperor Taizu of Song still refused to make him a commissioner or chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 況今邊戍未撤，警報時聞，若諸將一一遂其所求，志得意滿，猝有緩急，孰肯效死？」

translations.literal: Moreover, the border garrisons have not yet been withdrawn and alarms are heard from time to time. If every general were given all he asked for and grew complacent and satisfied, who in a sudden emergency would be willing to die in service?"
translations.idiomatic: The frontier garrisons are still in place and alarms still sound. If every general got everything he wanted and grew smug, who would die for the realm when crisis struck?"

sentences.zh: 趙善湘以從官開閫，指授之功居多，日夜望執政。

translations.literal: Zhao Shanxiang, as a member of the imperial clan, opened a commandery headquarters; his direction had contributed greatly to the victory, and day and night he looked toward appointment as chief councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shanxiang of the imperial clan had opened a command headquarters and had directed much of the campaign; he constantly hoped for a seat in the chief council.

sentences.zh: 彌遠曰：「天族於國有嫌，高宗有詔止許任從官，不許為執政。

translations.literal: Miyuan said, "The imperial clan bears a certain tension toward the state. Gaozong issued an edict permitting them only to hold posts as members of the clan entourage, not to serve as chief councillors.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan said, "The imperial clan is always a delicate matter for the state. Gaozong decreed that clansmen might hold clan offices but not serve as chief councillors.

sentences.zh: 紹熙末，慶元初，因汝愚、彥逾有定策功，是以權宜行之。

translations.literal: At the end of Shaoxi and the beginning of Qingyuan, because Ruyu and Yanyue had merit in settling the succession, it was done as an expedient.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Shaoxi and the start of Qingyuan, Zhao Ruyu and Ye Yanyue were given council posts only because they had helped settle the succession—an exceptional case.

sentences.zh: 某與善湘姻家，則又豈敢。」

translations.literal: As for me, being related by marriage to Shanxiang, how could I dare?"
translations.idiomatic: As I am related to Shanxiang by marriage, how could I possibly agree?"

sentences.zh: 彌遠親密友周鑄、兄彌茂、甥夏周篆皆寄以腹心，人皆謂三人者必顯貴，然鑄老於布衣，彌茂以執政恩入流，周篆以捧香恩補官，俱止訓武郎而已。

translations.literal: Miyuan entrusted his intimate friend Zhou Zhu, his elder brother Miyuan Mao, and his nephew Xia Zhouzhuan with his innermost confidence. All said the three were sure to rise to high honor, yet Zhu remained in plain robes until old age; Mao entered the civil roster through the chief councillor's favor; Zhouzhuan received office through the incense-offering favor—and all stopped at the rank of Instructor in Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan trusted his close friend Zhou Zhu, his brother Miyuan Mao, and his nephew Xia Zhouzhuan with his deepest secrets. Everyone expected them to rise high, yet Zhu died a commoner, Mao entered office only through the chief councillor's privilege, and Zhouzhuan through a minor court favor—and none rose above Instructor in Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，彌遠既誅韓侂胄，相寧宗十有七年。

translations.literal: From the beginning, after Miyuan had executed Han Tuozhou, he served as chief councillor to Ningzong for seventeen years.
translations.idiomatic: After executing Han Tuozhou, Miyuan had served as Ningzong's chief councillor for seventeen years.

sentences.zh: 迨寧宗崩，廢濟王，非寧宗意。

translations.literal: When Ningzong died, he deposed the Prince of Ji—this was not Ningzong's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong died he deposed the Prince of Ji, though that had not been Ningzong's wish.

sentences.zh: 立理宗，又獨相九年，擅權用事，專任儉壬。

translations.literal: He installed Lizong and then served alone as chief councillor for nine more years, monopolizing power and relying exclusively on petty flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: He installed Lizong and ruled alone for nine more years, hoarding power and filling office with sycophants.

sentences.zh: 理宗德其立己之功，不思社稷大計，雖台諫言其奸惡，弗恤也。

translations.literal: Lizong was grateful for his merit in establishing him on the throne and gave no thought to the great design of the altars; though the censorate spoke of his wickedness, he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Lizong was grateful that Miyuan had put him on the throne and ignored the welfare of the realm; even when censors denounced Miyuan's crimes, the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 彌遠死，寵渥猶優其子孫，厥後為制碑銘，以「公忠翊運，定策元勳」題其首。

translations.literal: When Miyuan died, favor still showered his descendants; later a stele inscription was composed with the heading "Loyal in public service, supporting the dynasty, founding meritocrat in settling the succession."
translations.idiomatic: After Miyuan's death his descendants were still richly favored, and a stele was later erected bearing the title "Loyal servant who upheld the dynasty and founding meritocrat of the succession."

sentences.zh: 濟王不得其死，識者群起而論之，而彌遠反用李知孝、梁成大等以為鷹犬，於是一時之君子貶竄斥逐，不遺餘力雲。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ji did not meet a natural death; men of insight rose up to discuss it, yet Miyuan instead employed Li Zhixiao, Liang Chengda, and others as hawks and hounds, and so the gentlemen of the age were demoted, banished, and driven out with unsparing effort.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ji had died under suspicious circumstances, and thoughtful men protested, yet Miyuan used Li Zhixiao, Liang Chengda, and others as his enforcers, banishing and persecuting the leading scholars of the day without mercy.

sentences.zh: 鄭清之

translations.literal: Zheng Qingzhi
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qingzhi

sentences.zh: 鄭清之，字德源，慶元之鄞人。

translations.literal: Zheng Qingzhi, styled Deyuan, was a native of Yin in Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qingzhi, whose style was Deyuan, was a native of Yin in Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初名燮，字文叔。

translations.literal: His original name was Xie, styled Wenshu.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally been named Xie, with the style Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 少從樓昉學，能文，樓鑰亟加稱賞。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Lou Fang and was skilled at writing; Lou Yue repeatedly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under Lou Fang and showed literary talent; Lou Yue often praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰二年，入太學。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiatai, he entered the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiatai (1202) he entered the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 十年，登進士第，調峽州教授。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as professor in Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jiatai he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed professor in Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帥趙方嚴重，靳許可，清之往白事，為置酒，命其子範、葵出拜，方掖清之無答拜，且曰：「他日願以二子相累。」

translations.literal: The commander Zhao Fang was stern and sparing of approval. When Qingzhi went to report on business, Fang set out wine and ordered his sons Fan and Kui to come out and bow. Fang raised Qingzhi so that he need not return the bow, and said, "In days to come I wish to entrust my two sons to you."
translations.idiomatic: The commander Zhao Fang was stern and slow to praise anyone. When Qingzhi came to report on affairs, Fang gave a banquet and had his sons Fan and Kui come out to bow. Fang raised Qingzhi so he need not bow in return and said, "One day I hope to leave my two sons in your care."

sentences.zh: 湖北茶商群聚暴橫，清之白總領何炳曰：「此輩精悍，宜籍為兵，緩急可用。」

translations.literal: In Hubei, tea merchants gathered in bands and acted violently. Qingzhi reported to the intendant He Bing: "These men are tough and capable; they should be registered as soldiers for use in emergencies."
translations.idiomatic: In Hubei, tea merchants had banded together and grown violent. Qingzhi told the intendant He Bing, "These men are tough and capable; they should be enrolled as troops for emergencies."

sentences.zh: 炳亟下召募之令，趨者雲集，號曰「茶商軍」，後多賴其用。

translations.literal: Bing quickly issued a recruitment order; those who hurried to answer gathered like clouds. They were called the "Tea Merchant Army," and later much use was made of them.
translations.idiomatic: Bing quickly issued a recruitment order, and volunteers flocked in. They were called the "Tea Merchant Army" and proved valuable in later campaigns.

sentences.zh: 調湖、廣總所準備差遣、國子監書庫官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to preparatory assignment at the Hu-Guang General Office and to Librarian of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to preparatory duty at the Hu-Guang General Office and made librarian of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷國子學錄。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was promoted to Recorder of the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Jiatai he was promoted to Recorder of the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 丞相史彌遠與清之謀廢濟國公，事見《皇子竑傳》。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan and Qingzhi plotted to depose the Prince of Ji; the matter is treated in the biography of Prince Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan and Qingzhi plotted to depose the Prince of Ji; see the biography of Prince Huo.

sentences.zh: 俄以清之兼魏惠憲王府教授，遷宗學諭，遷太學博士，皆仍兼教授。

translations.literal: Soon Qingzhi was made concurrently Professor of the Establishment of Prince Weihuixian, promoted to Instructor of the Imperial Clan School, then to Doctor of the Imperial University—all while still holding his professorship.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made professor at the establishment of Prince Weihuixian, then Instructor of the Imperial Clan School, then Doctor of the Imperial University, retaining his teaching posts throughout.

sentences.zh: 甯宗崩，丞相入定策，詔旨皆清之所定。

translations.literal: When Ningzong died, the chief councillor entered to settle the succession; all the edicts were drafted by Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong died, the chief councillor settled the succession, and Qingzhi drafted all the edicts.

sentences.zh: 理宗即帝位，授諸王宮大小學教授，遷宗學博士、宗正寺丞兼權工部郎、兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: When Lizong took the throne, Qingzhi was appointed Professor of the Greater and Lesser Schools of the Princes' Establishment, promoted to Doctor of the Imperial Clan School, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court with acting duty as Secretary in the Ministry of Works, and concurrently Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Lizong ascended the throne, Qingzhi was made professor at the schools for imperial clansmen, then Doctor of the Imperial Clan School, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court with acting duty in the Ministry of Works, and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝問外人因閣子庫進絲履有謗議，清之言：「禁中服用頗事新潔者。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked about outside criticism over silk shoes presented through the Inner Storehouse. Qingzhi said, "Within the palace, dress tends rather toward what is fresh and clean."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about public criticism over silk shoes supplied through the Inner Storehouse. Qingzhi said, "Within the palace there is already a taste for what is fresh and new in dress."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「故事，月進鞵數兩，朕非敝不易，何由致謗？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "By precedent, only a few pairs of shoes are presented each month. I do not change them until they are worn out—how could this draw criticism?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "By precedent only a few pairs are sent each month. I do not replace them until they are worn out—how could that invite slander?"

sentences.zh: 清之奏：「孝宗繼高宗，故儉德易章，陛下繼甯考，故儉德難著。

translations.literal: Qingzhi memorialized: "Xiaozong succeeded Gaozong, so frugal virtue was easy to display. Your Majesty succeeds Ningzong, so frugal virtue is hard to make manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi replied, "Xiaozong followed Gaozong, so his frugality was easy to show. Your Majesty follows Ningzong, so frugality is harder to make visible.

sentences.zh: 甯考自奉如寒士，衣領重浣，革舄屢補，今欲儉德著聞，須過於甯考方可。」

translations.literal: Ningzong supported himself like a poor scholar—collars washed again and again, leather shoes repeatedly patched. If you wish frugal virtue to be known abroad, you must surpass Ningzong."
translations.idiomatic: Ningzong lived like a poor scholar, washing his collars again and again and patching his leather shoes. If you wish your frugality to be widely known, you must go beyond what Ningzong did."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 寶慶元年，改兼兵部兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官，遷起居郎，仍兼史官、說書、樞密院編修官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoqing, he was transferred to concurrent duty in the Ministry of War, as Compiler of the National History Academy and Reviser of the Veritable Records Academy; he was promoted to Recorder of the Emperor's Actions, still holding his posts as historiographer, lecturer, and Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoqing (1225) he was given concurrent duty in the Ministry of War and on the National History and Veritable Records, was promoted to Recorder of the Emperor's Actions, and kept his posts as historiographer, lecturer, and compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，權工部侍郎，暫權給事中，進給事中，升兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was made Acting Vice Minister of Works, temporarily Acting Supervising Secretary, then promoted to Supervising Secretary, and advanced to Associate Compiler of the National History and Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became Acting Vice Minister of Works, then Acting and finally full Supervising Secretary, and was promoted to Associate Compiler of the National History and Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年，遷翰林學士、知制誥兼侍讀，升兼修國史實錄院修撰、端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoding, he was transferred to Hanlin Academician, Drafting Proclamations and Concurrent Lecturer, and was promoted to additionally serve as Compiler of the National History and Veritable Records, Academician of the Duanming Hall, and Deputy Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoding (1228) he was made Hanlin academician, in charge of drafting proclamations and concurrent lecturer; he was then promoted to compiler of the National History and Veritable Records, Duanming Hall academician, and deputy signatory at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年，授參知政事兼簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor and Deputy Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed vice grand councillor and deputy signatory at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，兼同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he held concurrent appointment as Associate Controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was given concurrent duty as associate controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，彌遠卒，命清之為右丞相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Miyuan died, and Qingzhi was ordered to be Right Grand Councillor and Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Miyuan died, and Qingzhi was appointed right grand councillor and commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 端平元年，上既親總庶政，赫然獨斷，而清之亦慨然以天下為己任，召還真德秀、魏了翁、崔與之、李𡌴、徐僑、趙汝談、尤焴、游似、洪咨夔、王遂、李宗勉、杜范、徐清叟、袁甫、李韶，時號「小元祐。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Duanping, the emperor having personally taken charge of all affairs and ruling with conspicuous independent decision, Qingzhi also took the empire upon himself with resolve, recalling Zhen Dexiu, Wei Liaoweng, Cui Yuzhi, Li Hui, Xu Qiao, Zhao Rutan, You Yu, You Si, Hong Zikui, Wang Sui, Li Zongmian, Du Fan, Xu Qingsou, Yuan Fu, and Li Shao—at the time called the "Little Yuanyou."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duanping (1234), with the emperor now personally directing affairs and ruling with firm independent authority, Qingzhi likewise took the empire's welfare as his own charge. He recalled Zhen Dexiu, Wei Liaoweng, Cui Yuzhi, Li Hui, Xu Qiao, Zhao Rutan, You Yu, You Si, Hong Zikui, Wang Sui, Li Zongmian, Du Fan, Xu Qingsou, Yuan Fu, and Li Shao—a group known at the time as the "Little Yuanyou."

sentences.zh: 大者相繼為宰輔，惟與之終始辭不至，遣逸如劉宰、趙蕃皆見旌異。

translations.literal: The greater among them successively became chief ministers; only Yuzhi from beginning to end declined and would not come. Recluses such as Liu Zai and Zhao Fan were all specially honored.
translations.idiomatic: The leading figures among them successively entered the highest councils; only Cui Yuzhi consistently declined and never came to court. Recluses such as Liu Zai and Zhao Fan were likewise singled out for special honors.

sentences.zh: 是時金雖亡而入洛之師大潰。

translations.literal: At this time, although Jin had perished, the army entering Luoyang suffered a great rout.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Jin had already fallen, yet the Song forces entering Luoyang suffered a disastrous rout.

sentences.zh: 二年，上疏乞罷，不可，拜特進、左丞相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the second year, he memorialized begging to resign; this was not granted, and he was appointed Special Advancement, Left Grand Councillor and Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he memorialized asking to be relieved of office. The request was denied, and he was appointed special advancement, left grand councillor, and commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，霖雨大風，四疏丐去。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, torrential rains and great winds; he submitted four memorials begging to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year, as torrential rains and violent winds struck, he submitted four memorials asking to leave office.

sentences.zh: 九月，禋祀雷變，請益力。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, at the great sacrificial service there was a thunder portent; he petitioned all the more forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, when thunder accompanied the great sacrificial rites, he pressed his resignation request with still greater urgency.

sentences.zh: 乃授觀文殿大學士、醴泉觀使兼侍讀，四疏控辭，依舊大學士、提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Grand Academician of the Guanwen Hall, Commissioner of the Liquan View and Concurrent Lecturer; four memorials controlled his acceptance of the words of appointment; he remained Grand Academician and was made Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made grand academician of the Guanwen Hall, commissioner of the Liquan View, and concurrent lecturer; after four memorials declining the appointment, he was retained as grand academician and made superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 及聞邊警，密疏：「恐陛下憂悔太過，以汩清明之躬，累剛大之志。」

translations.literal: When he heard of border alarms, in a secret memorial he said: "I fear Your Majesty's excessive sorrow and regret may cloud a clear and bright person and encumber a firm and resolute will."
translations.idiomatic: When border alarms reached him, he submitted a secret memorial: "I fear that excessive sorrow and regret may cloud Your Majesty's clarity and weigh down your firm and resolute resolve."

sentences.zh: 嘉熙三年，封申國公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaxi, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiaxi (1239) he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣中使賜禦書「輔德明謨之閣」，賜楮十萬緡為築室，乃日與賓客門生相羊山水間。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an imperial emissary was dispatched to bestow the imperial calligraphy "Pavilion of Assisting Virtue and Clarifying Counsel," and one hundred thousand strings of paper currency for building a residence; then daily with guests and students he wandered among mountains and waters.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year an imperial emissary brought the emperor's own inscription for the "Pavilion of Assisting Virtue and Clarifying Counsel," along with one hundred thousand strings of paper currency to build a residence. Thereafter he spent his days wandering among hills and streams with guests and disciples.

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年，依前觀文殿大學士、醴泉觀使兼侍讀，屢辭不允，拜少保、觀文殿大學士、醴泉觀使兼侍讀，進封衛國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunyou, as before Grand Academician of the Guanwen Hall, Commissioner of the Liquan View and Concurrent Lecturer—repeatedly declined, not granted—he was appointed Junior Guardian, Grand Academician of the Guanwen Hall, Commissioner of the Liquan View and Concurrent Lecturer, and advanced to Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunyou (1244), though he repeatedly declined reappointment as grand academician of the Guanwen Hall, Liquan View commissioner, and concurrent lecturer, he was made junior guardian with those same posts and was advanced to Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 趣入見，有旨賜第。

translations.literal: He was urged to enter for an audience; an order granted him a residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned for an audience and granted an imperial residence.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，上壽畢，亦疏丐歸，不允。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, after felicitations on the emperor's birthday were completed, he also memorialized begging to return home; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, after celebrating the emperor's birthday, he memorialized asking to retire home; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 拜少傅，依前觀文殿大學士、醴泉觀使兼侍讀，進封越國公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Preceptor, as before Grand Academician of the Guanwen Hall, Liquan View Commissioner and Concurrent Lecturer, and advanced to Duke of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed junior preceptor, retained his posts as Guanwen Hall grand academician, Liquan View commissioner, and concurrent lecturer, and was advanced to Duke of Yue.

sentences.zh: 居無何，喪其子士昌，決意東還，又不許。

translations.literal: Before long after settling there, he mourned the death of his son Shichang; resolved to return east, again not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his son Shichang died; resolved to return east, he was once again refused permission.

sentences.zh: 拜少師、奉國軍節度使，依前醴泉觀使兼侍讀、越國公，賜玉帶，更賜第於西湖之漁莊。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Master, Military Commissioner of the Fengguo Army, as before Liquan View Commissioner and Concurrent Lecturer and Duke of Yue; granted a jade belt; additionally granted a residence at the Fishing Lodge on West Lake.
translations.idiomatic: He was made junior master and military commissioner of the Fengguo Army, kept his posts as Liquan View commissioner and concurrent lecturer, and retained his title as Duke of Yue; he was granted a jade belt and a new residence at the Fishing Lodge on West Lake.

sentences.zh: 進讀《仁皇訓典》，謂：「仁祖之仁厚，發為英明，故能修明紀綱，而無寬弛不振之患；

translations.literal: In lecturing on the Instructions of the Renhuang, he said: "Renzu's humaneness and magnanimity issued forth as brilliance and clarity, and thus he was able to rectify and clarify institutions, without the affliction of laxity and failure to rouse action;
translations.idiomatic: While lecturing on the Instructions of Emperor Renzong, he said: "Emperor Renzong's humaneness and magnanimity blossomed into brilliance and clarity, enabling him to strengthen institutions without the danger of lax indulgence and slack governance;

sentences.zh: 孝宗之英明，本于仁厚，故能涵養士氣，而無矯勵峭刻之習。

translations.literal: Xiaozong's brilliance and clarity rooted in humaneness and magnanimity, and thus he was able to nourish the spirit of scholars, without the habit of forced striving and harsh severity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong's brilliance and clarity were rooted in humaneness and magnanimity, enabling him to nourish the spirit of the scholar-official class without the habit of forced striving and harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 蓋仁厚、英明二者相須，此仁祖、孝宗所以為盛也。」

translations.literal: Humaneness and magnanimity and brilliance and clarity—the two mutually require each other; this is why Renzu and Xiaozong were flourishing."
translations.idiomatic: Humaneness and brilliance depend on each other; that is why the reigns of Renzong and Xiaozong were so flourishing."

sentences.zh: 帝褒諭之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and commended him.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜太保，力辭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed Grand Guardian; he forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was offered the post of grand guardian but declined forcefully.

sentences.zh: 故事，許回授子孫，清之請追封高祖洽，帝從之，蓋異恩也。

translations.literal: By precedent, one was permitted to transfer honors to descendants; Qingzhi requested posthumous enfeoffment for his great-grandfather Qia, and the emperor assented—this was an exceptional grace.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent an official could transfer honors to descendants; Qingzhi asked that his great-grandfather Qia be posthumously enfeoffed, and the emperor agreed—an exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 七年，拜太傅、右丞相兼樞密使、越國公。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was appointed Grand Preceptor, Right Grand Councillor and Commissioner of Military Affairs, Duke of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed grand preceptor, right grand councillor, commissioner of military affairs, and Duke of Yue.

sentences.zh: 中使及門，清之方放浪湖山，寓僧刹，竟夕不歸。

translations.literal: When the imperial emissary reached his gate, Qingzhi was just roving idly among lakes and mountains, lodging at a Buddhist monastery, and did not return all night.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial emissary arrived at his door, Qingzhi was off enjoying the lakes and mountains, staying at a Buddhist monastery, and did not return until dawn.

sentences.zh: 詰旦內引，叩頭辭免，帝勉諭有外間所不及知者。

translations.literal: At daybreak he was ushered into the palace; he kowtowed begging to decline; the emperor urged him on, saying there were matters outsiders could not know.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he was summoned within the palace, where he kowtowed and begged to be excused; the emperor urged him to accept, saying there were matters unknown to those outside.

sentences.zh: 甫退，則中使接踵而至。

translations.literal: He had just withdrawn when imperial emissaries arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he withdrawn when imperial emissaries arrived one after another.

sentences.zh: 或請更化改元，清之曰：「改元，天子之始事，更化，朝廷之大端，漢事已非古，然不因易相而為之。」

translations.literal: Some requested renewal of governance and changing the reign title; Qingzhi said: "Changing the reign title is the emperor's initial act; renewing governance is a great turning point for the court. Han precedents are not ancient, yet neither is done merely because the chief minister is changed."
translations.idiomatic: When some urged a change of reign title and renewal of governance, Qingzhi said, "Changing the reign title is the emperor's inaugural act; renewing governance is a great turning point for the court. Han precedents are hardly ancient models, yet in any case neither should be done simply because the chief minister has changed."

sentences.zh: 帝以邊事為憂，詔趙葵以樞使視師，陳靴以知樞密院事帥湖、廣，二人方辭遜，會清之再相，力主之，科降辟置無所留難，葵、靴遂往。

translations.literal: The emperor, anxious over border affairs, ordered Zhao Kui as commissioner of military affairs to inspect the armies, and Chen Wei as controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs to command Hu and Guang; the two men were just declining modestly when Qingzhi became chief minister again, strongly supported them, and in appointments and commissions raised no obstacles—Kui and Wei then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Troubled by border affairs, the emperor ordered Zhao Kui, as commissioner of military affairs, to take command in the field and Chen Wei, as controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs, to lead forces in Hu and Guang. Both were hesitating to accept when Qingzhi returned as chief minister, strongly backed them, and cleared every appointment without obstruction—whereupon Kui and Wei set out.

sentences.zh: 於是戰于泗水、渦口、木庫，皆以捷聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon at Sishui, Wokou, and Muku they fought, and in every case victory was reported.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon battles were fought at Sishui, Wokou, and Muku, and in every case victory was reported.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜太師、左丞相兼樞密使，辭太師不拜，依前太傅。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was appointed Grandee, Left Grand Councillor and Commissioner of Military Affairs; he declined the grandeeship and did not accept it, remaining as before Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was offered grandee and left grand councillor with the military commission; he declined the grandeeship and remained grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 每謂天下之財困於養兵，兵費困於生券，思所以變通之，遇調戍防邊，命樞屬量遠近以便其道塗，時緩急以次其遣發。

translations.literal: He often said the empire's finances were strained by maintaining troops, and military expenses strained by pay certificates; he thought how to change and adapt this. When troops were mobilized for garrison duty on the frontier, he ordered staff of the Bureau of Military Affairs to measure distances near and far to ease their routes, and according to urgency to sequence their dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: He often observed that the empire's finances were strained by maintaining troops and that military costs were further burdened by pay certificates; he sought ways to reform the system. When troops were mobilized for frontier garrison duty, he ordered Bureau of Military Affairs staff to calculate distances so routes could be eased and dispatches sequenced according to urgency.

sentences.zh: 又議移歲調兵屯以戍淮面，並軍分頭目以節廩稍，先移鎮江策勝一軍屯泗水，公私便之。

translations.literal: He also proposed transferring yearly mobilized garrison troops to guard the Huai front, consolidating army units and dividing commanders to regulate rations and stipends; first he moved the Cesheng Army from Zhenjiang to garrison at Sishui, to the convenience of public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed shifting yearly mobilized garrison troops to guard the Huai front, consolidating units and dividing command to regulate rations and stipends. First he moved the Cesheng Army from Zhenjiang to garrison Sishui—a change that benefited both the state and the people.

sentences.zh: 諸路虧鹽，執其事者破家以償，清之核其犯科者追理，掛誤者悉蠲之，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: On the various circuits salt deficits were incurred; those in charge of the matter ruined their families to make repayment. Qingzhi investigated those who had violated regulations and pursued recovery, and fully remitted those who had been implicated by error; very many were wholly preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: Where salt deficits occurred on the various circuits, officials in charge often ruined their families trying to make repayment. Qingzhi investigated those who had truly violated regulations and pursued recovery, while fully remitting debts owed through error—sparing a great many families ruin.

sentences.zh: 沿江算舟之賦素重，清之次第停罷，如池之雁氵義有大法場之目，其錢分隸諸司，清之奏罷其並緣漁取者，蓋數倍公家之入，合分隸者從朝廷償之。

translations.literal: The tax on boats along the river had always been heavy; Qingzhi stopped and abolished it step by step. For example, at Yanqi in Chi there was the designation Great Dharma Field; its revenues were divided among various offices. Qingzhi memorialized to abolish those who used this as a pretext to fish for gain—amounting to several times the public revenue—and those offices that should have received shares were compensated by the court.
translations.idiomatic: The tax on boats along the Yangzi had long been heavy; Qingzhi abolished it in stages. At Yanqi in Chi Prefecture, for example, revenues under the designation Great Dharma Field had been divided among various offices. Qingzhi memorialized to abolish the exactions that used this as a pretext to fish for profit—amounting to several times the state's proper revenue—and had the affected offices compensated from the court.

sentences.zh: 報下，清之方與客飲，舉杯曰：「今日飲此酒殊快！」

translations.literal: When the reply came down, Qingzhi was just drinking with guests; he raised his cup and said: "Today drinking this wine is especially delightful!"
translations.idiomatic: When the reply arrived, Qingzhi was drinking with guests; he raised his cup and said, "This wine tastes especially fine today!"

sentences.zh: 四上謝事之章。

translations.literal: He submitted four memorials thanking the throne and requesting to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted four memorials thanking the throne and asking to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 十年，進《十龜元吉箴》，一持敬，二典學，三崇儉，四力行，五能定，六明善，七謹微，八察言，九惜時，十務實。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he presented the "Ten Tortoises Primordial Auspicious Admonitions": first, maintaining reverence; second, honoring learning; third, esteeming frugality; fourth, exerting effort; fifth, being able to settle; sixth, discerning goodness; seventh, being careful in minute matters; eighth, examining words; ninth, cherishing time; tenth, seeking what is solid and real.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he presented the "Ten Tortoises Primordial Auspicious Admonitions": maintaining reverence; honoring learning; esteeming frugality; exerting effort; being able to settle affairs; discerning goodness; being careful in minute matters; examining words; cherishing time; and seeking what is solid and real.

sentences.zh: 疏奏：「敬天之怒易，敬天之休難，天怒可憂而以為易，天休可喜而以為難，何哉？

translations.literal: In his memorial he stated: "Revering Heaven's anger is easy; revering Heaven's favor is difficult. Heaven's anger should cause concern yet is treated as easy; Heaven's favor should bring joy yet is treated as difficult—why?
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial he wrote: "It is easy to revere Heaven's anger but hard to revere Heaven's favor. Heaven's anger should cause concern, yet men treat it lightly; Heaven's favor should bring joy, yet men treat it with difficulty—why?

sentences.zh: 蓋憂則懼心生，懼則怒可轉而為休；

translations.literal: Because when one is worried, fear arises in the heart; when one fears, anger can turn into favor;
translations.idiomatic: Because worry gives rise to fear, and fear can turn Heaven's anger into favor;

sentences.zh: 喜則玩心生，玩則休或轉而為怒。」

translations.literal: when one is pleased, a playful heart arises; when one plays, favor may turn into anger."
translations.idiomatic: but pleasure gives rise to complacency, and complacency can turn Heaven's favor back into anger."

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，命史官書之，賜詔獎諭。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, ordered the historiographers to record it, and bestowed an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, ordered the historiographers to record it, and issued an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 十一年，十疏乞罷政，皆不許。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, ten memorials begging to resign from office—all were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he submitted ten memorials asking to leave office; all were denied.

sentences.zh: 拜太師，力辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grandee; he forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the post of grandee but declined forcefully.

sentences.zh: 有事於明堂，有旨閤門給扶掖二人，再賜玉帶，令服以朝。

translations.literal: When there were rites at the Bright Hall, an order directed the Gate of Reception to provide two attendants to support him; a jade belt was again bestowed, and he was ordered to wear it at court.
translations.idiomatic: When rites were held at the Bright Hall, an order directed the Gate of Reception to provide two attendants to support him; he was again granted a jade belt and ordered to wear it at court.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁酉，退朝感寒疾，危甚，猶以未得雪為憂。

translations.literal: On dingyou in the eleventh month, after retiring from court he contracted a cold illness; critically ill, he still worried that snow had not yet fallen.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou in the eleventh month, after leaving court he fell gravely ill with a cold; even in his critical state he still worried that snow had not yet fallen.

sentences.zh: 俄大雪，起曰：「百官賀雪，上必甚喜。」

translations.literal: Soon heavy snow fell; he rose and said: "The officials will congratulate on the snow; the emperor must be greatly pleased."
translations.idiomatic: Soon heavy snow fell; he roused himself and said, "The officials will offer congratulations on the snow; the emperor must be greatly pleased."

sentences.zh: 命掬雪床前觀之。

translations.literal: He ordered snow scooped up before his bed for him to look at.
translations.idiomatic: He had snow scooped up and brought to his bedside so he could look at it.

sentences.zh: 累奏乞罷政，不允，奏不已，拜太傅、保甯軍節度使充醴泉觀使，進封齊國公致仕。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he memorialized begging to resign from office; not granted; memorializing without cease, he was appointed Grand Preceptor, Military Commissioner of the Baoning Army as Commissioner of the Liquan View, and advanced to Duke of Qi with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized asking to leave office, but when his petitions went unanswered he was finally appointed grand preceptor, military commissioner of the Baoning Army, and commissioner of the Liquan View, advanced to Duke of Qi, and granted retirement.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺表聞，帝震悼，輟朝三日，特贈尚書令，追封魏郡王，賜諡忠定。

translations.literal: He died; his final memorial was reported; the emperor was shaken and grieved, suspended court for three days, specially posthumously granted Minister of the Masters of Writing, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wei Commandery, and granted the posthumous title "Loyal and Settled."
translations.idiomatic: When he died and his final memorial reached the throne, the emperor was deeply shaken and grieved, suspended court for three days, posthumously granted him Minister of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffed him posthumously as Prince of Wei Commandery, and gave him the posthumous title Loyal and Settled.

sentences.zh: 清之不好立異，湯巾嘗論事侵清之，及清之再相，巾求去，清之曰：「己欲作君子，使誰為小人。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi did not like to stand apart in opposition. Tang Jin once discussed affairs in a way that encroached on Qingzhi; when Qingzhi became chief minister again, Jin requested to leave. Qingzhi said: "If you wish to be the gentleman, who is to be the petty man?"
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi did not like to stand apart in opposition. Tang Jin had once criticized him in debate; when Qingzhi returned as chief minister, Jin asked to leave. Qingzhi said, "If you insist on being the gentleman, who is left to play the villain?"

sentences.zh: 力挽留之。

translations.literal: He forcefully detained him and kept him.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed him forcefully to stay.

sentences.zh: 徐清叟嘗論列清之，乃引之共政。

translations.literal: Xu Qingsou had once memorialized criticizing Qingzhi; Qingzhi then brought him in to share in government.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qingsou had once memorialized against Qingzhi; Qingzhi then brought him into the government to serve alongside him.

sentences.zh: 趙葵視師年餘，乞罷，上未有以處之，清之曰：「非使作相不足以酬勞，陛下豈以臣故耶？

translations.literal: Zhao Kui inspected the armies for more than a year and begged to resign; the emperor had no way to place him. Qingzhi said: "Only making him chief minister is insufficient to reward his labors—is Your Majesty withholding this because of me?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kui had inspected the armies for more than a year and asked to be relieved; the emperor did not know how to reward him. Qingzhi said, "Only making him chief minister would adequately reward his service—is Your Majesty holding back because of me?

sentences.zh: 臣必不因葵來遽引退，臣願為左，使葵居右。」

translations.literal: I will certainly not hastily withdraw because Kui comes; I wish to be on the left and have Kui on the right."
translations.idiomatic: I will certainly not withdraw hastily because Kui is coming; I am willing to serve on the left and let Kui serve on the right."

sentences.zh: 上訖從之，然葵竟不果來。

translations.literal: The emperor finally assented, yet Kui in the end did not come after all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally agreed, but Kui never did come to court.

sentences.zh: 清之代言奏對，多不存稿，有《安晚集》六十卷。

translations.literal: When Qingzhi drafted responses and memorials on the emperor's behalf, he mostly did not keep drafts; he had the Collected Works of Anwan in sixty juan.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhi drafted imperial responses and memorials, he usually kept no drafts; his Collected Works of Anwan ran to sixty juan.

sentences.zh: 清之自與彌遠議廢濟王竑，立理宗，駸駸至宰輔，然端平之間召用正人，清之之力也。

translations.literal: From the time Qingzhi together with Miyuan deliberated on deposing Prince Ji Gong and installing Lizong, he gradually advanced to chief minister; yet during the Duanping period the recall and employment of upright men was Qingzhi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Qingzhi joined Miyuan in deposing Prince Ji and installing Lizong, he had gradually risen to chief minister; yet the recall of upright men during the Duanping period was largely Qingzhi's work.

sentences.zh: 至再相，則年齒衰暮，政歸妻子，而閑廢之人或因緣以賄進，為世所少雲。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister again, his years were declining into old age; government fell to his wife and children, and idle and dismissed men sometimes used connections to advance through bribery—this the age held in little esteem.
translations.idiomatic: When he became chief minister a second time, he was already advanced in years; government fell to his wife and children, and idle or dismissed men sometimes used connections to buy their way back into office—conduct the age held in little esteem.

sentences.zh: 史嵩之

translations.literal: Shi Songzhi
translations.idiomatic: Shi Songzhi

sentences.zh: 史嵩之，字子由，慶元府鄞人。

translations.literal: Shi Songzhi, styled Ziyou, was a native of Yin in Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Songzhi, whose style was Ziyou, was a native of Yin in Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年進士，調光化軍司戶參軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as Registrar of the Revenue Section in Guanghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiading (1220) he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of the revenue section in Guanghua Army.

sentences.zh: 十六年，差充京西、湖北路制置司準備差遣。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was assigned as preparatory commissioner on the Jingxi-Hubei Circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was assigned as preparatory commissioner on the Jingxi-Hubei Circuit Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 十七年，升幹辦公事。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was promoted to Administrative Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to administrative clerk.

sentences.zh: 寶慶三年，主管機宜文字，通判襄陽府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoqing, he was put in charge of confidential documents and made Vice Prefect of Xiangyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoqing (1227) he was put in charge of confidential documents and appointed vice prefect of Xiangyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年，以經理屯田，襄陽積谷六十八萬，加其官，權知棗陽軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoding, for managing garrison fields he accumulated six hundred eighty thousand units of grain at Xiangyang; his rank was increased, and he was made Acting Prefect of Zaoyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoding (1228), for managing garrison fields he accumulated six hundred eighty thousand units of grain at Xiangyang; his rank was raised and he was made acting prefect of Zaoyang Army.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷軍器監丞兼權知棗陽軍，尋兼制置司參議官。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to Assistant Director of the Armory and concurrently Acting Prefect of Zaoyang Army; soon after he additionally served as Advisory Official on the Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to assistant director of the Armory and concurrently acting prefect of Zaoyang Army; soon after he also served as advisory official on the Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 三年，棗陽屯田成，轉兩官。

translations.literal: In the third year, the garrison fields at Zaoyang were completed; he was transferred two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the garrison fields at Zaoyang were completed, he was promoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 以明堂恩，封鄞縣男，賜食邑。

translations.literal: By grace of the Bright Hall rites, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yin County and granted a fief for sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: By grace of the Bright Hall rites, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yin County and granted a fief for sustenance.

sentences.zh: 以直秘閣、京西轉運判官兼提舉常平兼安撫制置司參議官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Access to the Secretariat, Transport Commissioner of Jingxi, concurrently Intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries and Advisory Official on the Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed direct access to the Secretariat, transport commissioner of Jingxi, concurrently intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries and advisory official on the Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷大理少卿兼京西、湖北制置副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and concurrently Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Jingxi and Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to vice minister of justice and concurrently deputy pacification commissioner of Jingxi and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 五年，加大理卿兼權刑部侍郎，升制置使兼知襄陽府，賜便宜指揮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was additionally made Minister of Justice and Acting Vice Minister of Punishments, promoted to Pacification Commissioner and concurrently Prefect of Xiangyang, and granted discretionary command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was additionally made minister of justice and acting vice minister of punishments, promoted to pacification commissioner and concurrently prefect of Xiangyang, and granted discretionary command.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷刑部侍郎，仍舊職。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments, retaining his former duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to vice minister of punishments while retaining his former duties.

sentences.zh: 臣熟慮根本，周思利害，甘受遲鈍之譏，思出萬全之計。

translations.literal: "Your subject has thoroughly considered fundamentals and broadly weighed benefits and harms, willingly accepting the reproach of sluggishness in order to devise a plan of complete safety."
translations.idiomatic: "Your subject has thoroughly weighed fundamentals and broadly considered benefits and harms, willingly accepting the charge of sluggishness in order to devise a plan of complete safety."

sentences.zh: 荊襄連年水潦螟蝗之災，饑饉流亡之患，極力振救，尚不聊生，徵調既繁，夫豈堪命？

translations.literal: "Jing and Xiang have suffered year after year from floods and locust plagues, famine and the affliction of displaced people; though relief has been exerted to the utmost, life is still barely sustainable. Levies and mobilizations are already numerous—how can the people bear such commands?"
translations.idiomatic: "Jing and Xiang have suffered year after year from floods and locust plagues, famine, and mass displacement; though relief efforts have been pushed to the limit, the people can barely survive. Levies and mobilizations are already crushing—how can they bear more?"

sentences.zh: 其勢必至於主戶棄業以逃亡，役夫中道而竄逸，無歸之民，聚而為盜，饑饉之卒，未戰先潰。

translations.literal: "The situation will inevitably reach the point where household heads abandon their occupations and flee, conscript laborers bolt midway, people with nowhere to return gather and become bandits, and troops weakened by famine collapse before battle."
translations.idiomatic: "The situation will inevitably reach the point where household heads abandon their occupations and flee, conscripts desert midway, displaced people gather into bandit bands, and famine-weakened troops collapse before battle even begins."

sentences.zh: 當此之際，正恐重貽宵旰之慮矣。

translations.literal: "At such a moment, I truly fear adding anew to Your Majesty's cares late into the night and early at dawn."
translations.idiomatic: "At such a moment, I truly fear adding anew to Your Majesty's sleepless cares."

sentences.zh: 兵民，陛下之兵民也，片紙調發，東西惟命。

translations.literal: "Soldiers and people are Your Majesty's soldiers and people; with a single sheet of paper for mobilization, east or west they obey commands."
translations.idiomatic: "Soldiers and people are Your Majesty's soldiers and people; at a single written order for mobilization, they go east or west as commanded."

sentences.zh: 然事關根本，願計其成，必計其敗，既慮其始，必慮其終，謹而審之，與二三大臣深計而熟圖之。

translations.literal: "Yet the matter touches fundamentals; I wish that success be calculated together with failure, that the beginning be weighed together with the end—considering carefully and examining closely, and planning deeply and thoroughly with the chief ministers."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet the matter touches fundamentals; I ask that success be weighed together with failure, the beginning together with the end—considering carefully and examining closely, and planning deeply and thoroughly with the chief ministers."

sentences.zh: 若夫和好之與進取，決不兩立。

translations.literal: "As for peace and alliance versus advance and seizure—they absolutely cannot stand together."
translations.idiomatic: "Peace and alliance on the one hand and advance and seizure on the other absolutely cannot stand together."

sentences.zh: 臣受任守邊，適當事會交至之沖，議論紛紜之際。

translations.literal: "Your subject received appointment to guard the frontier, just as affairs converged at a critical juncture and opinions were clamorous."
translations.idiomatic: "Your subject received appointment to guard the frontier just as affairs converged at a critical juncture and opinions were clamorous."

sentences.zh: 雷同和附，以致誤國，其罪當誅；

translations.literal: "Echoing others in agreement and going along to the point of misleading the state—such a crime deserves execution;"
translations.idiomatic: "Echoing others in agreement to the point of misleading the state—such a crime deserves execution;"

sentences.zh: 確守不移之愚，上迕丁寧之旨，罪亦當誅。

translations.literal: "the folly of firmly holding without shifting, above violating repeated admonitions—this crime also deserves execution."
translations.idiomatic: "the folly of holding firm without shifting, in defiance of repeated admonitions—that crime also deserves execution."

sentences.zh: 迕旨則止於一身，誤國則及天下。

translations.literal: "Violating the imperial will affects only one person; misleading the state affects the whole empire."
translations.idiomatic: "Violating the imperial will affects only one person; misleading the state affects the whole empire."

sentences.zh: 丞相鄭清之亦以書言勿為異同，嵩之力求去。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Zheng Qingzhi also wrote advising against creating differences; Songzhi forcefully sought to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Zheng Qingzhi also wrote advising against creating divisions; Songzhi pressed forcefully to resign.

sentences.zh: 朝陵之使未還，而諸軍數道並進，復上疏乞黜罷，權兵部尚書，不拜。

translations.literal: The envoys to the imperial tombs had not yet returned when armies advanced on several routes together; he again memorialized begging to be dismissed, was appointed Acting Minister of War, and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys to the imperial tombs had not yet returned when armies advanced on several routes together; he again memorialized asking to be dismissed, was offered acting minister of war, and declined to accept.

sentences.zh: 乞祠，進寶章閣直學士，提舉太平宮，歸養田裏。

translations.literal: He requested a sinecure, was promoted to Direct Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, made Superintendent of the Taiping Palace, and returned to his fields to support his parents.
