translations.idiomatic: He requested a sinecure, was promoted to direct academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, made superintendent of the Taiping Palace, and returned to his fields to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 尋以華文閣直學士知隆興府兼江西安撫使。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made Direct Academician of the Huawen Pavilion, Prefect of Longxing Prefecture, and concurrently Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made direct academician of the Huawen Pavilion, prefect of Longxing Prefecture, and concurrently Jiangxi pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝自師潰，始悔不用嵩之言，召見，力辭，權刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Since the rout of the army, the emperor began to regret not having used Songzhi's advice; he summoned him for an audience; Songzhi forcefully declined; he was appointed Acting Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: After the army's rout, the emperor began to regret not having heeded Songzhi's advice; he summoned him for an audience, but Songzhi declined forcefully and was appointed acting minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 引見，疏言結人心、作士氣、核實理財等事。

translations.literal: At his presentation he memorialized on binding people's hearts, rousing the spirit of scholars, verifying and solidifying financial administration, and other matters.
translations.idiomatic: At his presentation he memorialized on winning people's hearts, rousing the spirit of the scholar-official class, verifying and solidifying financial administration, and other matters.

sentences.zh: 且言：「今日之事，當先自治，不可專恃和議。」

translations.literal: He also stated: "In affairs today, self-governance must come first; one cannot rely solely on peace negotiations."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "In affairs today, self-governance must come first; one cannot rely solely on peace negotiations."

sentences.zh: 乞祠，以前職知平江府，以母病乞侍醫藥，不俟報可而歸。

translations.literal: He requested a sinecure, was appointed with his former rank as Prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture; because his mother was ill he begged to attend her with medicine, and returned without awaiting approval.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a sinecure and was appointed with his former rank as prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture; when his mother fell ill he begged leave to attend her with medicine and returned without awaiting approval.

sentences.zh: 進寶章閣學士、淮西制置使兼沿江制置副使兼知鄂州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, Pacification Commissioner of Huai West, concurrently Deputy Pacification Commissioner Along the River, and Prefect of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, pacification commissioner of Huai West, concurrently deputy pacification commissioner along the river, and prefect of E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既內引，賜便宜指揮，兼湖、廣總領兼淮西安撫使。

translations.literal: After he was ushered into the palace, he was granted discretionary command, and additionally served as General Intendant of Hu and Guang and Huai West Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After he was summoned within the palace, he was granted discretionary command and additionally served as general intendant of Hu and Guang and Huai West pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙元年，進華文閣學士、京西荊湖安撫制置使，依舊沿江制置副使兼節制光、黃、蘄、舒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaxi, he was promoted to Academician of the Huawen Pavilion and Jingxi-Jinghu Pacification Commissioner, remaining as before Deputy Pacification Commissioner Along the River and concurrently controlling Guang, Huang, Qi, and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaxi (1237) he was promoted to academician of the Huawen Pavilion and Jingxi-Jinghu pacification commissioner, remaining deputy pacification commissioner along the river and concurrently controlling Guang, Huang, Qi, and Shu.

sentences.zh: 乞免兼總領，從之。

translations.literal: He requested to be relieved of the concurrent general intendancy; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be relieved of the concurrent general intendancy, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 廬州圍解，詔獎諭之。

translations.literal: When the siege of Luzhou was lifted, an edict commended and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege of Luzhou was lifted, an edict commended him.

sentences.zh: 以明堂恩，進封伯，加食邑。

translations.literal: By the grace of the Bright Hall ceremony, he was advanced to Baron and given additional income lands.
translations.idiomatic: On account of the Bright Hall favor, he was promoted to baron and granted additional income lands.

sentences.zh: 條奏江、淮各三事，又陳十難，又言江陵非孟珙不可守，乞勉諭之。

translations.literal: He submitted memorials itemizing three matters each for the Yangtze and Huai regions, again presented ten difficulties, again stated that Chingling could not be held without Meng Kung, and begged that Meng be encouraged and instructed.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorials setting forth three matters each for the Yangtze and Huai regions, presented ten difficulties, and argued that Chingling could not be held without Meng Kung, begging that Meng be encouraged to remain.

sentences.zh: 漢陽受攻，嵩之帥師發江陵，奏誅張可大，竄盧普、李士達，以其棄城也。

translations.literal: When Hanyang came under attack, Songzhi led troops setting out from Chingling; he memorialized for the execution of Chang K'o-ta and banished Lu P'u and Li Shih-ta for abandoning the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Hanyang came under attack, Songzhi led troops out from Chingling, memorialized for the execution of Chang K'o-ta, and banished Lu P'u and Li Shih-ta for having abandoned their posts.

sentences.zh: 二年，黃州圍解，降詔獎諭，拜端明殿學士，職任依舊，恩數視執政，進封奉化郡侯，加食邑。

translations.literal: In the second year, when the siege of Huang Prefecture was lifted, an edict descended commending and instructing him; he was appointed Academician of the Tuanming Hall, his duties remaining as before, his favors equaling those of chief administrators; he was advanced to Marquis of Fenghua Commandery and given additional income lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when the siege of Huang Prefecture was lifted, an edict commended him; he was appointed academician of the Tuanming Hall with his duties unchanged and favors equal to those of chief ministers, was promoted to marquis of Fenghua Commandery, and granted additional income lands.

sentences.zh: 詔入覲，拜參知政事，督視東西、荊湖南北、江西路軍馬，鄂州置司，兼督視淮南西路軍馬兼督視光、蘄、黃、夔、施州軍馬，加食邑。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him for audience; he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor, supervisor of armies of East and West, Chinghunnan-north and Chinghu, and Kiangsi circuits; a commission was established at O Prefecture, and he additionally supervised Huainan West Route armies and concurrently supervised armies of Kuang, Ch'i, Huang, K'uei, and Shih Prefectures; his income lands were increased.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, he was appointed vice grand councillor and placed in charge of the armies of the East and West, Chinghu, and Kiangsi circuits, with his headquarters at O Prefecture; he additionally supervised the Huainan West Route armies and the forces of Kuang, Ch'i, Huang, K'uei, and Shih, and was granted additional income lands.

sentences.zh: 城黃州。

translations.literal: He fortified Huang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Huang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十一月，復光州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Kuang Prefecture was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Kuang Prefecture was recovered.

sentences.zh: 十二月，復滁州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Ch'u Prefecture was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Ch'u Prefecture was recovered.

sentences.zh: 三年，授宣奉大夫、右丞相兼樞密、都督兩淮四川京西湖北軍馬，進封公，加食邑，兼督江西、湖南軍馬，改都督江、淮、京、湖、四川軍馬。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was granted the rank of Hsüan-feng Grandee, Right Chief Councillor concurrently Director of the Privy Council, and Grand Supervisor of the armies of the Two Huai, Szechuan, Chingxi, and Hupai; he was advanced to Duke and given additional income lands; additionally he supervised Kiangsi and Hunan armies; his title was changed to Grand Supervisor of the armies of the Yangtze, Huai, Ching, Hu, and Szechuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, he was granted the rank of Hsüan-feng Grandee and appointed right chief councillor concurrently director of the privy council and grand supervisor of the armies of the Two Huai, Szechuan, Chingxi, and Hupai; he was promoted to duke and granted additional income lands, additionally supervised the armies of Kiangsi and Hunan, and his title was revised to grand supervisor of the Yangtze, Huai, Ching, Hu, and Szechuan armies.

sentences.zh: 薦士三十有二人，其後董槐、吳潛皆號賢相。

translations.literal: He recommended thirty-two scholars; afterward Tung Huai and Wu Ch'ien were both hailed as worthy chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended thirty-two scholars; afterward Tung Huai and Wu Ch'ien were both acclaimed as worthy chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 復信陽，以督府米拯淮民之饑。

translations.literal: Hsin-yang was recovered; with grain from the supervisory headquarters he rescued the Huai people from famine.
translations.idiomatic: Hsin-yang was recovered, and grain from the supervisory headquarters was used to relieve famine among the Huai people.

sentences.zh: 六月，復襄陽，嵩之言：「襄陽雖復，未易守。」

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Hsiang-yang was recovered; Songzhi stated: "Though Hsiang-yang has been recovered, it will not be easy to hold."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Hsiang-yang was recovered; Songzhi said, "Though Hsiang-yang has been recovered, it will not be easy to defend."

sentences.zh: 自是邊境多以捷聞，降詔獎諭。

translations.literal: From then on the frontier frequently reported victories; edicts descended commending and instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the frontier frequently reported victories, and edicts commended him.

sentences.zh: 四年，乞祠，趣召奏事，轉三官，依前右丞相兼樞密使，眷顧特隆，賜齎無虛日。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he begged a sinecure; urgently summoned to report on affairs, he was transferred three ranks, remaining as before Right Chief Councillor concurrently Director of the Privy Council; imperial favor was unusually great, and gifts were bestowed not a day in vain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he requested a sinecure but was urgently summoned to report on affairs; he was promoted three ranks and remained right chief councillor concurrently director of the privy council; imperial favor was unusually great, and gifts were bestowed day after day.

sentences.zh: 久旱，乞解機政。

translations.literal: After prolonged drought, he begged to be relieved of policy-making duties.
translations.idiomatic: During a prolonged drought, he asked to be relieved of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 地震，屢疏乞罷免，皆不許。

translations.literal: An earthquake occurred; he repeatedly submitted memorials begging dismissal—all were refused.
translations.idiomatic: After an earthquake, he repeatedly submitted memorials asking to be dismissed, but all were refused.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年，進《玉斧箴》。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ch'un-yu, he presented the Admonition of the Jade Axe.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ch'un-yu (1241), he presented the Admonition of the Jade Axe.

sentences.zh: 安南入貢，不用正朔，嵩之議用范仲淹卻西夏書例，以不敢聞於朝還之。

translations.literal: Annam sent tribute without using the dynastic calendar; Songzhi proposed applying Fan Chung-yen's precedent in returning Hsi Hsia's letters, returning it on grounds of not daring to let the court know of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Annam sent tribute without acknowledging the dynastic calendar, Songzhi proposed following Fan Chung-yen's precedent in rejecting Western Hsia correspondence, and had the tribute returned on the ground that the court should not be apprised of it.

sentences.zh: 二年，進高、孝、光、甯帝《紀》，《孝宗經武要略》，《甯宗實錄》、《日曆》，《會要》、《玉牒》，進金紫光祿大夫，加食邑。

translations.literal: In the second year, he presented the Annals of the Kao, Hsiao, Kuang, and Ning Emperors, the Essentials of Emperor Hsiao-tsung's Military Governance, the Veritable Records and Daily Calendar of Emperor Ning-tsung, the Institutional Compendium, and the Imperial Genealogy; he was advanced to Grandee of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle and given additional income lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he presented the annals of the Kao, Hsiao, Kuang, and Ning emperors, the Essentials of Emperor Hsiao-tsung's Military Governance, the Veritable Records and Daily Calendar of Emperor Ning-tsung, the Institutional Compendium, and the Imperial Genealogy; he was promoted to grandee of the golden seal and purple girdle and granted additional income lands.

sentences.zh: 是冬，封永國公，加食邑。

translations.literal: That winter, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yung Kingdom and given additional income lands.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, he was enfeoffed as duke of Yung Kingdom and granted additional income lands.

sentences.zh: 四年，遭父喪，起復右丞相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he suffered his father's death; recalled from mourning, he was again Right Chief Councillor concurrently Director of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when his father died, he was recalled from mourning to serve again as right chief councillor concurrently director of the privy council.

sentences.zh: 累賜手詔，遣中使趣行。

translations.literal: Handwritten edicts were repeatedly bestowed; palace envoys were sent to urge him to take up office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly sent handwritten edicts and dispatched palace envoys to hurry him back to office.

sentences.zh: 於是太學生黃愷伯、金九萬、孫翼鳳等百四十四人，武學生翁日善等六十七人，京學生劉時舉、王元野、黃道等九十四人，宗學生與寰等三十四人，建昌軍學教授盧鉞，皆上書論嵩之不當起復，不報。

translations.literal: Thereupon one hundred forty-four students of the Imperial Academy, including Huang K'ai-po, Chin Chiu-wan, and Sun I-feng; sixty-seven students of the Military Academy, including Weng Jih-shan; ninety-four students of the Capital Academy, including Liu Shih-chü, Wang Yüan-yeh, and Huang Tao; thirty-four students of the Princes' Academy, including Yü Huan; and Lu Yüeh, professor of the Chien-ch'ang Prefecture school—all submitted memorials arguing that Songzhi ought not be recalled from mourning; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon one hundred forty-four Imperial Academy students, including Huang K'ai-po, Chin Chiu-wan, and Sun I-feng; sixty-seven Military Academy students, including Weng Jih-shan; ninety-four Capital Academy students, including Liu Shih-chü, Wang Yüan-yeh, and Huang Tao; thirty-four Princes' Academy students, including Yü Huan; and Lu Yüeh, professor of the Chien-ch'ang Prefecture school—all submitted memorials arguing that Songzhi should not be recalled from mourning, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 將作監徐元傑奏對及劉鎮上封事，帝意頗悟。

translations.literal: Hsu Yüan-chieh of the Directorate of Palace Buildings answered at audience, and Liu Chên submitted a sealed memorial; the emperor's mind was somewhat awakened.
translations.idiomatic: After Hsu Yüan-chieh of the directorate of palace buildings answered at audience and Liu Chên submitted a sealed memorial, the emperor's mind was somewhat changed.

sentences.zh: 初，嵩之從子璟卿嘗以書諫曰：

translations.literal: Earlier, Songzhi's nephew Ching Ch'ing had once remonstrated by letter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Songzhi's nephew Ching Ch'ing had once remonstrated with him in a letter, saying:

sentences.zh: 伯父秉天下之大政，必辦天下之大事；

translations.literal: "Uncle, holding the great governance of the empire, must accomplish the great affairs of the empire;"
translations.idiomatic: "Uncle, holding the great governance of the empire, must accomplish the empire's great affairs;"

sentences.zh: 膺天下之大任，必能成天下之大功。

translations.literal: "bearing the great charge of the empire, must be able to achieve the great merit of the empire."
translations.idiomatic: "bearing the empire's great charge, must be able to achieve its great merit."

sentences.zh: 比所行浸不克終，用人之法，不待舉削而改官者有之，譴責未幾而旋蒙敘理者有之，丁難未幾而遽被起復者有之。

translations.literal: Of late what you undertake gradually fails to reach completion; in your method of employing men, there are those promoted to office without awaiting recommendation and scrutiny, those soon after censure who again receive reinstatement, and those scarcely into mourning who are suddenly recalled from it.
translations.idiomatic: Of late what you undertake gradually fails to reach completion; in your method of employing men, some are promoted without awaiting recommendation and scrutiny, some censured one day and reinstated the next, and some scarcely in mourning before being suddenly recalled.

sentences.zh: 借曰有非常之才，有不次之除，醲恩異賞，所以收拾人才，而不知斯人者果能運籌帷幄、獻六奇之策而得之乎？

translations.literal: Granting that there are extraordinary talents receiving extraordinary appointments—rich favor and special rewards to gather men of ability—yet do you know whether such men truly won their posts by scheming within the tent and offering the six wondrous stratagems?
translations.idiomatic: Granting that extraordinary talents receive extraordinary appointments—rich favor and special rewards to gather men of ability—do you know whether such men truly won their posts by scheming within the tent and offering the six wondrous stratagems?

sentences.zh: 抑亦獻賂幕賓而得之乎？

translations.literal: Or did they win them by offering bribes as staff retainers?
translations.idiomatic: Or did they win them by offering bribes as staff retainers?

sentences.zh: 果能馳身鞍馬，效一戰之勇而得之乎？

translations.literal: Did they truly win them by charging on horseback and displaying the valor of a single battle?
translations.idiomatic: Did they truly win them by charging on horseback and displaying the valor of a single battle?

sentences.zh: 抑亦效顰奴僕而得之乎？

translations.literal: Or did they win them by aping frowns like menials and servants?
translations.idiomatic: Or did they win them by aping frowns like menials and servants?

sentences.zh: 徒聞包苴公行，政出多門，便嬖私昵，狼狽萬狀，祖宗格法，壞於今日也。

translations.literal: One hears only that bribes are openly exchanged, policy issues from many gates, favorites and private intimates run rampant in every disgraceful way, and the ancestral regulations are ruined today.
translations.idiomatic: One hears only that bribes are openly exchanged, policy issues from many hands, favorites and private intimates run rampant in every disgraceful way, and the ancestral regulations are being ruined today.

sentences.zh: 自開督府，東南民力，困於供需，州縣倉卒，匱于應辦，輦金帛，輓芻粟，絡繹道路，曰一則督府，二則督府，不知所幹者何事，所成者何功！

translations.literal: Since the supervisory headquarters was opened, the strength of the people in the southeast has been exhausted by supply and demand; prefectures and counties are hard pressed and depleted in meeting requisitions; gold and silks are carted, fodder and grain hauled, crowding the roads—"first the supervisory headquarters, second the supervisory headquarters"—and no one knows what business is being done or what achievement is being accomplished!
translations.idiomatic: Since the supervisory headquarters was opened, the strength of the people in the southeast has been exhausted by supply and demand; prefectures and counties are hard pressed and depleted in meeting requisitions; gold, silks, fodder, and grain crowd the roads—"first the supervisory headquarters, second the supervisory headquarters"—and no one knows what business is being done or what achievement is being accomplished!

sentences.zh: 近聞蜀川不守，議者多歸退師于鄂之失。

translations.literal: Recently I hear that Szechuan is not being held; many in discussion attribute it to the error of withdrawing troops at O.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I hear that Szechuan is not being held; many attribute it to the error of withdrawing troops at O.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 分戍列屯，備邊禦戎，首尾相援，如常山之蛇。

translations.literal: Garrisons were distributed in camps, guarding the frontier and repelling barbarians, head and tail aiding each other like the serpent of Ch'ang-shan.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons were distributed in camps to guard the frontier and repel invaders, head and tail aiding each other like the serpent of Ch'ang-shan.

sentences.zh: 維揚則有趙葵，廬江則有杜伯虎，金陵則有別之傑。

translations.literal: At Wei-yang there was Chao K'uei, at Lu-chiang Tu Po-hu, at Chin-ling Pieh Chih-chieh.
translations.idiomatic: At Wei-yang there was Chao K'uei, at Lu-chiang Tu Po-hu, and at Chin-ling Pieh Chih-chieh.

sentences.zh: 為督府者，宜據鄂渚形勢之地，西可以援蜀，東可以援淮，北可以鎮荊湖。

translations.literal: For one holding the supervisory headquarters, he ought to occupy the strategic ground at O-chu: westward he could aid Szechuan, eastward aid the Huai, northward secure Ching and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The holder of the supervisory headquarters ought to occupy the strategic ground at O-chu: from there he could aid Szechuan to the west, the Huai to the east, and secure Ching and Hu to the north.

sentences.zh: 不此之圖，盡損藩籬，深入堂奧，伯父謀身自固之計則安，其如天下蒼生何！

translations.literal: Instead of planning thus, you have wholly stripped away the outer defenses and penetrated deep into the inner chambers—Uncle, your plan to secure yourself is safe enough, but what of the living masses under heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Instead of planning thus, you have wholly stripped away the outer defenses and penetrated deep into the inner chambers—Uncle, your plan to secure yourself may be safe enough, but what of the living masses under heaven!

sentences.zh: 是以饑民叛將，乘虛搗危，侵軼於沅、湘，搖盪於鼎、澧。

translations.literal: Hence starving people and rebel generals, seizing the void to strike at danger, have raided Yüan and Hsiang and shaken Ting and Li.
translations.idiomatic: Hence starving people and rebel generals, seizing the opportunity to strike, have raided Yüan and Hsiang and shaken Ting and Li.

sentences.zh: 為江陵之勢苟孤，則武昌之勢未易守；

translations.literal: If the position at Chingling should stand alone, then the position at Wuch'ang will not be easy to hold;
translations.idiomatic: If the position at Chingling stands alone, then the position at Wuch'ang will not be easy to hold;

sentences.zh: 刑湖之路稍警，則江、浙之諸郡焉得高枕而臥？

translations.literal: if the routes of Ching and Hu are slightly alarmed, how can the prefectures of Kiang and Che sleep with pillows high?
translations.idiomatic: if the routes of Ching and Hu are slightly alarmed, how can the prefectures of Kiang and Che sleep in peace?

sentences.zh: 況殺降失信，則前日徹疆之計不可復用矣；

translations.literal: Moreover, killing those who surrendered and breaking faith—then the plan of the other day to withdraw frontiers cannot be used again;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, killing those who surrendered and breaking faith means the plan of the other day to withdraw frontiers cannot be used again;

sentences.zh: 內地失護，則前日清野之策不可復施矣。

translations.literal: the inner lands losing protection—then the strategy of the other day to clear the countryside cannot be applied again.
translations.idiomatic: the inner lands losing protection means the strategy of the other day to clear the countryside cannot be applied again.

sentences.zh: 此隙一開，東南生靈特幾上之肉耳。

translations.literal: Once this gap is opened, the living masses of the southeast are no more than meat upon the chopping block.
translations.idiomatic: Once this gap is opened, the living masses of the southeast will be no more than meat upon the chopping block.

sentences.zh: 則宋室南渡之疆土，惡能保其金甌之無闕也。

translations.literal: Then how can the territory of the Sung house since the southern crossing preserve its golden bowl without breach?
translations.idiomatic: Then how can the territory of the Sung house since the southern crossing preserve its integrity without breach?

sentences.zh: 盍早為之圖，上以寬九重宵旰之憂，下以慰雙親朝夕之望。

translations.literal: Why not plan for this early—above to ease the Ninefold Height's anxiety from dawn to dusk, below to comfort your parents' hope from morning to evening?
translations.idiomatic: Why not plan for this early—above to ease the emperor's anxiety from dawn to dusk, below to comfort your parents' hope from morning to evening?

sentences.zh: 不然，師老財殫，績用不成，主憂臣辱，公論不容。

translations.literal: Otherwise, troops will grow weary and funds exhausted, achievements will not be completed, the ruler will worry and the minister be shamed, and public opinion will not tolerate it.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, troops will grow weary and funds exhausted, achievements will not be completed, the ruler will worry and the minister be shamed, and public opinion will not tolerate it.

sentences.zh: 萬一不畏強禦之士，繩以《春秋》之法，聲其討罪不效之咎，當此之時，雖優遊菽水之養，其可得乎？

translations.literal: Should men who fear not the powerful bind you by the law of the Spring and Autumn Annals and proclaim the fault of campaigning without effect—at such a time, even the leisurely nurture of bean and water, could you obtain it?
translations.idiomatic: Should men who fear not the powerful bind you by the law of the Spring and Autumn Annals and proclaim the fault of campaigning without effect—at such a time, could you even enjoy the leisurely nurture of bean and water?

sentences.zh: 異日國史載之，不得齒于趙普開國勳臣之列，而乃廁于蔡京誤國亂臣之後，遺臭萬年，果何面目見我祖於地下乎？

translations.literal: When the national history records it in days to come, you will not rank among the founding merit ministers like Chao P'u, but will be placed after the state-misleading traitors like Ts'ai Ching—leaving a stench for ten thousand years; with what face can you meet our ancestors beneath the ground?
translations.idiomatic: When the national history records it in days to come, you will not rank among the founding merit ministers like Chao P'u, but will be placed after the state-misleading traitors like Ts'ai Ching—leaving a stench for ten thousand years; with what face can you meet our ancestors beneath the ground?

sentences.zh: 人謂禍起蕭牆，危如朝露，此愚所痛心疾首為伯父苦口極言。

translations.literal: Men say disaster rises within the curtained wall and danger is like morning dew—this is what I, in deepest grief, bitterly speak to Uncle with utmost earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: Men say disaster rises within the curtained wall and danger is like morning dew—this is what I, in deepest grief, speak to Uncle with utmost earnestness.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，莫若盡去在幕之群小，悉召在野之君子，相與改弦易轍，戮力王事，庶幾失之東隅，收之桑榆矣。

translations.literal: For the plan of today, nothing is better than wholly removing the petty men in the staff, summoning all the gentlemen in retirement, together changing strings and altering the track, joining strength in the king's affairs—then perhaps what was lost at the eastern corner may be recovered at the mulberry sunset.
translations.idiomatic: For the plan of today, nothing is better than wholly removing the petty men in the staff, summoning all the gentlemen in retirement, together changing course and joining strength in the king's affairs—then perhaps what was lost at the eastern corner may be recovered at the mulberry sunset.

sentences.zh: 如其視失而不知救，視非而不知革，薰蕕同器，駑驥同櫪，天下大勢，駸駸日趨於危亡之域矣。

translations.literal: If you see loss yet know not how to rescue, see wrong yet know not how to reform, put fragrant orchid and foul weed in the same vessel and slow nags with swift steeds in the same manger—the great trend of the empire will day by day hasten toward the realm of peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: If you see loss yet know not how to rescue, see wrong yet know not how to reform, put fragrant orchid and foul weed in the same vessel and slow nags with swift steeds in the same manger—the great trend of the empire will day by day hasten toward peril and ruin.

sentences.zh: 伯父與璟卿，親猶父子也，伯父無以少年而忽之，則吾族幸甚！

translations.literal: Uncle and Ching Ch'ing are as close as father and son; Uncle, do not dismiss this because I am young—then our clan will be greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: Uncle and Ching Ch'ing are as close as father and son; Uncle, do not dismiss this because I am young—then our clan will be greatly fortunate!

sentences.zh: 天下生靈幸甚！

translations.literal: The living masses under heaven will be greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: The living masses under heaven will be greatly fortunate!

sentences.zh: 我祖宗社稷幸甚！

translations.literal: Our ancestral altars and state will be greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestral altars and state will be greatly fortunate!

sentences.zh: 居無何，璟卿暴卒，相傳嵩之致毒雲。

translations.literal: Before long, Ching Ch'ing died suddenly; rumor had it that Songzhi had caused his death by poison.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Ching Ch'ing died suddenly; rumor had it that Songzhi had caused his death by poison.

sentences.zh: 嵩之為公論所不容，居閑十有三年。

translations.literal: Songzhi was not tolerated by public opinion and lived in retirement for thirteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi was not tolerated by public opinion and lived in retirement for thirteen years.

sentences.zh: 寶祐四年春，授觀文殿大學士，加食邑。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Pao-yu, he was appointed Grand Academician of the Kuan-wen Hall and given additional income lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year of Pao-yu (1256), he was appointed grand academician of the Kuan-wen Hall and granted additional income lands.

sentences.zh: 八月癸巳卒，遺表上，帝輟朝，贈少師、安德軍範度使，進封魯國公，諡忠簡，以家諱改諡莊肅。

translations.literal: On the kuei-ssu day of the eighth month he died; his final memorial was submitted; the emperor suspended court; he was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor and Military Commissioner of An-te Army, advanced to Duke of Lu Kingdom, given the posthumous title Chung-chien, and the posthumous title was changed to Chuang-su because of a family taboo.
translations.idiomatic: On the kuei-ssu day of the eighth month he died; his final memorial was submitted; the emperor suspended court; he was posthumously granted junior preceptor and military commissioner of An-te Army, promoted to duke of Lu Kingdom, given the posthumous title Chung-chien, and the posthumous title was changed to Chuang-su because of a family taboo.

sentences.zh: 德祐初，以右正言徐直方言奪諡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Te-yu, on the memorial of Right Remonstrator Hsu Chih-fang, his posthumous title was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Te-yu, on the memorial of Right Remonstrator Hsu Chih-fang, his posthumous title was revoked.

sentences.zh: 董槐，字庭植，濠州定遠人。

translations.literal: Tung Huai, styled Ting-chih, was a native of Ting-yuan in Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tung Huai, whose style was Ting-chih, was a native of Ting-yuan in Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少喜言兵，陰讀孫武、曹操之書，而曰：「使吾得用，將汛掃中土以還天子。」

translations.literal: In youth he delighted in speaking of warfare and secretly read the books of Sun Wu and Ts'ao Ts'ao, saying: "If I were given employment, I would sweep the central lands clean and restore them to the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: In youth he delighted in speaking of warfare and secretly read the books of Sun Wu and Ts'ao Ts'ao, saying, "If I were given employment, I would sweep the central lands clean and restore them to the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 槐貌甚偉，廣顙而豐頤，又美髯，論事慷慨，自方諸葛亮、周瑜。

translations.literal: Huai's appearance was very imposing—broad forehead and full cheeks, and a handsome beard; discussing affairs he was impassioned and compared himself to Chu-ko Liang and Chou Yü.
translations.idiomatic: Huai had a very imposing appearance—broad forehead, full cheeks, and a handsome beard; when discussing affairs he was impassioned and compared himself to Chu-ko Liang and Chou Yü.

sentences.zh: 父永，遇槐嚴，聞其自方，怒而嘻曰：「不力學，又自喜大言，此狂生耳，吾弗願也。」

translations.literal: His father Yung, encountering Huai in severity and hearing him compare himself thus, angrily laughed and said: "You do not study hard, yet delight in grand talk—this is a mad youth; I want no part of it."
translations.idiomatic: His father Yung, encountering Huai in severity and hearing him compare himself thus, angrily laughed and said, "You do not study hard, yet delight in grand talk—this is a mad youth; I want no part of it."

sentences.zh: 槐心愧，乃益自摧折，學于永嘉葉師雍。

translations.literal: Huai felt ashamed at heart and thereupon humbled himself all the more, studying under Yeh Shih-yung of Yung-chia.
translations.idiomatic: Huai felt ashamed at heart and thereupon humbled himself all the more, studying under Yeh Shih-yung of Yung-chia.

sentences.zh: 聞輔廣者，朱熹之門人，復往從廣，廣歎其善學。

translations.literal: Hearing that Fu Kuang was a disciple of Chu Hsi, he again went to follow Kuang; Kuang sighed at his excellence in learning.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Fu Kuang was a disciple of Chu Hsi, he again went to study under Kuang, who sighed at his excellence in learning.

sentences.zh: 嘉定六年，登進士第，調靖安主簿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chia-ting, he passed the chin-shih examination and was assigned as Recorder of Ching-an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chia-ting (1213), he passed the chin-shih examination and was assigned as recorder of Ching-an.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂去官。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his father and left office.

sentences.zh: 十四年，起為廣德軍錄事參軍，民有誣富人李桷私鑄兵結豪傑以應李全者，郡捕系之獄，槐察其枉，以白守，守曰：「為反者解說，族矣。」

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, recalled to serve as Judicial Assistant of Kuang-te Army; a commoner falsely accused the wealthy man Li Chüeh of privately casting weapons and joining heroes to respond to Li Ch'üan; the prefecture arrested and imprisoned him; Huai perceived the injustice and reported it to the prefect; the prefect said: "To plead for rebels is to bring extinction upon one's clan."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, he was recalled to serve as judicial assistant of Kuang-te Army; a commoner falsely accused the wealthy man Li Chüeh of privately casting weapons and joining heroes to respond to Li Ch'üan; the prefecture arrested and imprisoned him; Huai perceived the injustice and reported it to the prefect, who said, "To plead for rebels is to bring extinction upon one's clan."

sentences.zh: 槐曰：「吏明知獄有枉，而擠諸死地以傅於法：顧法豈謂諸被告者無論枉不枉，皆可殺乎？」

translations.literal: Huai said: "The official clearly knows the case is unjust, yet forces the accused toward death to fit the law—does the law truly mean that all defendants, whether wronged or not, may be killed?"
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "The official clearly knows the case is unjust, yet forces the accused toward death to fit the law—does the law truly mean that all defendants, whether wronged or not, may be killed?"

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect would not listen.

sentences.zh: 頃之，守以憂去，槐攝通判州事，歎曰：「桷誠枉，今不為出之，生無繇矣。」

translations.literal: Before long the prefect left office in grief; Huai acted as acting Vice Prefect and sighed: "Chüeh is truly wronged; if I do not release him now, he will have no way to live."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the prefect left office in grief; Huai acted as acting vice prefect and sighed, "Chüeh is truly wronged; if I do not release him now, he will have no way to live."

sentences.zh: 乃為翻其辭，明其不反，書上，卒脫桷獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reversed the charges, made clear that Chüeh had not rebelled, submitted a memorial, and in the end secured Chüeh's release from prison.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he reversed the charges, made clear that Chüeh had not rebelled, submitted a memorial, and in the end secured Chüeh's release from prison.

sentences.zh: 紹定二年，遷鎮江觀察推官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shao-ting, he was transferred to be Investigating Censor of Chên-chiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shao-ting (1229), he was transferred to be investigating censor of Chên-chiang.

sentences.zh: 明年春，入為主管刑部架閣文字。

translations.literal: The next spring he entered the capital as Supervisor of Documents in the Archives of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he entered the capital as supervisor of documents in the archives of the ministry of punishments.

sentences.zh: 秋，兼權禮兵部架閣，遷籍田令，特差權通判鎮江府。

translations.literal: In autumn he concurrently held acting charge of the Archives of the Ministries of Rites and War, was transferred to Registrar of the State Farms, and was specially assigned as acting Vice Prefect of Chên-chiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he concurrently held acting charge of the archives of the ministries of rites and war, was transferred to registrar of the state farms, and was specially assigned as acting vice prefect of Chên-chiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至州，會全叛，涉淮臨大江，大府急發州兵。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the prefecture, Ch'üan rebelled, crossed the Huai and approached the Great River; the superior prefecture urgently dispatched the prefectural troops.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the prefecture, Li Ch'üan rebelled, crossed the Huai and approached the Great River; the superior prefecture urgently dispatched the prefectural troops.

sentences.zh: 槐即日將兵濟江而西，全遁去，乃還。

translations.literal: Huai that same day led troops across the river westward; Ch'üan fled, and he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Huai that same day led troops across the river westward; Ch'üan fled, and he then returned.

sentences.zh: 五年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 端平三年，差通判蘄州，辭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tuan-p'ing, he was assigned as Vice Prefect of Ch'i Prefecture and declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tuan-p'ing (1236), he was assigned as vice prefect of Ch'i Prefecture and declined.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙元年，召赴都堂，遷宗正寺簿、出知常州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chia-hsi, he was summoned to the Imperial Secretariat, transferred to Registrar of the Imperial Clan Court, and sent out as Prefect of Ch'ang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chia-hsi (1237), he was summoned to the imperial secretariat, transferred to registrar of the imperial clan court, and sent out as prefect of Ch'ang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後三日，提點湖北刑獄。

translations.literal: Three days later he was made Judicial Intendant of Hupei.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he was made judicial intendant of Hupei.

sentences.zh: 常德軍亂，夜縱火而噪，守尉闖不出。

translations.literal: Ch'ang-te Army mutinied; at night they set fires and clamored; the prefect and commandant bolted their gates and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Ch'ang-te Army mutinied; at night they set fires and clamored; the prefect and commandant bolted their gates and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 槐騎從數人於火所，且問亂故。

translations.literal: Huai rode with a few followers to the place of fire and inquired into the cause of the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Huai rode with a few followers to the place of fire and inquired into the cause of the disorder.

sentences.zh: 亂者曰：「將軍馬彥直奪吾歲請，吾屬將責之償，不為亂也。」

translations.literal: The mutineers said: "General Ma Yen-chih seized our annual stipend; we intend to hold him accountable for repayment—we are not making rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers said, "General Ma Yen-chih seized our annual stipend; we intend to hold him accountable for repayment—we are not making rebellion."

sentences.zh: 槐坐馬上，召彥直斬馬前，亂者還入伍中，明日，乃捕首亂者七人戮諸市，而賻彥直之家。

translations.literal: Huai, seated on his horse, summoned Yen-chih and beheaded him before the horse; the mutineers returned to the ranks; the next day he arrested seven ringleaders and executed them in the market, and compensated Yen-chih's family.
translations.idiomatic: Huai, seated on his horse, summoned Yen-chih and beheaded him before the horse; the mutineers returned to the ranks; the next day he arrested seven ringleaders and executed them in the market, and compensated Yen-chih's family.

sentences.zh: 差充歸、峽、岳察訪使。

translations.literal: He was assigned to serve as Inspector of Kuei, Hsia, and Yüeh.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to serve as inspector of Kuei, Hsia, and Yüeh.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼權知常德府，尋兼軍器少監，依舊提點刑獄。

translations.literal: In the second year, he concurrently held acting charge as Prefect of Ch'ang-te Prefecture; soon after he additionally served as Vice Director of the Armory, while still holding judicial intendancy as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he concurrently held acting charge as prefect of Ch'ang-te Prefecture; soon after he additionally served as vice director of the armory, while still holding judicial intendancy as before.

sentences.zh: 三年，以直寶謨閣知江州兼都督府參謀。

translations.literal: In the third year, as Direct Attendant of the Pao-mo Pavilion he was made Prefect of Chiang Prefecture concurrently Staff Officer of the Grand Supervisory Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, as direct attendant of the Pao-mo Pavilion he was made prefect of Chiang Prefecture concurrently staff officer of the grand supervisory headquarters.

sentences.zh: 秋，流民渡江而來歸者十余萬，議者皆謂：「方軍興，郡國急儲粟，不暇食民也。」

translations.literal: In autumn, more than one hundred thousand refugees who had crossed the river to return home came; those in discussion all said: "With warfare underway, prefectures and commanderies urgently need stored grain and have no leisure to feed the people."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, more than one hundred thousand refugees who had crossed the river to return home came; those in discussion all said, "With warfare underway, prefectures and commanderies urgently need stored grain and have no leisure to feed the people."

sentences.zh: 槐曰：「民，吾民也，發吾粟振之，胡不可？」

translations.literal: Huai said: "The people are my people; to release my grain and relieve them—why may this not be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "The people are my people; to release my grain and relieve them—why may this not be done?"

sentences.zh: 至者如歸焉。

translations.literal: Those who arrived were as though returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Those who arrived were as though returning home.

sentences.zh: 當是時，宋與金為鄰國，而襄、漢、揚、楚之間，豪傑皆自相結以保其族，無賴者往往去為群盜。

translations.literal: At that time the Sung and the Chin were neighboring states; between Hsiang, Han, Yang, and Ch'u, heroes all joined one another to protect their clans, and ruffians often went off to become bandit gangs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Sung and the Chin were neighboring states; between Hsiang, Han, Yang, and Ch'u, local heroes all joined one another to protect their clans, and ruffians often went off to become bandit gangs.

sentences.zh: 浮光人翟全寓黃陂，有眾三千餘，稍出鹵掠。

translations.literal: Chai Ch'üan of Fu-kuang lodged at Huang-p'i with a following of more than three thousand and gradually went out on plundering raids.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Ch'üan of Fu-kuang lodged at Huang-p'i with a following of more than three thousand and gradually went out on plundering raids.

sentences.zh: 槐令客說下全，徙之陽烏洲，使雜耕蘄春間，又享賜之，用為裨將。

translations.literal: Huai had a guest persuade Ch'üan to submit; he moved him to Yang-wu Isle, had him farm mixed fields in the Ch'i-ch'un region, again feasted and rewarded him, and employed him as a deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Huai had a guest persuade Ch'üan to submit; he moved him to Yang-wu Isle, had him farm mixed fields in the Ch'i-ch'un region, again feasted and rewarded him, and employed him as a deputy general.

sentences.zh: 於是曹聰、劉清之屬皆來自歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ts'ao Ts'ung, Liu Ch'ing-chih, and their kind all came to submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Ts'ao Ts'ung, Liu Ch'ing-chih, and their kind all came to submit of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 四年，進直華文閣、知潭州、主管湖南安撫司公事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Hua-wen Pavilion, made Prefect of T'an Prefecture, and put in charge of the affairs of the Hunan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was promoted to direct attendant of the Hua-wen Pavilion, made prefect of T'an Prefecture, and put in charge of the affairs of the Hunan Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 方三邊急於守禦，督府日夜徵發，民且困，槐為畫策應之，令民不傷而軍須亦不匱。

translations.literal: Just as the three frontiers urgently needed defense, the supervisory headquarters requisitioned day and night and the people were growing distressed; Huai devised plans to meet the demands, so that the people were not harmed and military supplies were not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the three frontiers urgently needed defense, the supervisory headquarters requisitioned day and night and the people were growing distressed; Huai devised plans to meet the demands, so that the people were not harmed and military supplies were not exhausted.

sentences.zh: 淳祐二年，遷左司郎官，進直龍圖閣、沿江制置副使兼知江州、主管江西安撫司公事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Ch'un-yu, he was transferred to Left Department bureau officer and advanced to associate in the Chih Lung-t'u Pavilion, vice commissioner of the Yangtze River frontier command, concurrently prefect of Chiang Prefecture, and supervisor of the Kiangsi Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Ch'un-yu, he was transferred to Left Department bureau officer, promoted to associate in the Chih Lung-t'u Pavilion, vice commissioner of the Yangtze River frontier command, concurrently prefect of Chiang Prefecture, and supervisor of the Kiangsi Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 視其賦則吏侵甚，下教曰：「蒞州而吏猶為盜不自悔，吾且誅之！」

translations.literal: When he examined the taxes, official exactions were severe; he issued an instruction saying: "Having come to govern this prefecture, yet officials still steal without repenting—I shall execute them!"
translations.idiomatic: When he examined the taxes, he found official exactions were severe; he issued an instruction, saying, "Having come to govern this prefecture, yet officials still steal without repenting—I shall execute them!"

sentences.zh: 吏乃震恐，願自新。

translations.literal: The officials then trembled with fear and wished to reform themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The officials then trembled with fear and wished to reform themselves.

sentences.zh: 槐因除民患害，凡利有宜，弛以利民，惟恐不盡弛。

translations.literal: Huai therefore removed harms that afflicted the people; whenever a levy was suitable to relax, he relaxed it to benefit the people, fearing only that he might not relax enough.
translations.idiomatic: Huai therefore removed harms afflicting the people; whenever a levy was fit to relax, he relaxed it to benefit the people, fearing only that he might not relax enough.

sentences.zh: 大計軍實，常若敵且至。

translations.literal: He greatly reckoned military stores, always as though the enemy were about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted great attention to tallying military stores, always as though the enemy were about to arrive.

sentences.zh: 裨將盧淵凶猾不受命，斬以徇師，軍中肅然。

translations.literal: The deputy general Lu Yüan was fierce and crafty and would not obey orders; he was beheaded to admonish the army, and within the army there was solemn order.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy general Lu Yüan was fierce and crafty and refused to obey orders; he was beheaded as a warning to the army, after which discipline was restored throughout the ranks.

sentences.zh: 三年，進秘閣修撰。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was advanced to compiler in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, he was promoted to compiler in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 四年，召入奏事，遷權戶部侍即，賜紫，進集英殿修撰、沿江制置使、江東安撫使兼知建康府兼行宮留守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was summoned to the court to report on affairs, transferred to acting Vice Minister of Revenue, granted purple robes, and advanced to compiler in the Chi-ying Hall, commissioner of the Yangtze River frontier command, Eastern Kiang Pacification Commissioner, concurrently prefect of Chien-k'ang Prefecture and provisional custodian of the mobile palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was summoned to court to report on affairs, appointed acting Vice Minister of Revenue, granted purple robes, and promoted to compiler in the Chi-ying Hall, commissioner of the Yangtze River frontier command, Eastern Kiang pacification commissioner, concurrently prefect of Chien-k'ang, and provisional custodian of the mobile palace.

sentences.zh: 軍政弛弗治，乃為賞三等以教射，春秋教肄士卒坐作進退擊刺之技，歲餘盡為精兵。

translations.literal: Military administration was slack and untended; he therefore instituted three grades of reward to teach archery, and in spring and autumn instructed and drilled soldiers in the skills of sitting and rising, advancing and retreating, and thrusting and stabbing; after more than a year they all became elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: Military administration had grown lax; he instituted three grades of reward for archery and, in spring and autumn, drilled the soldiers in formations, advances and retreats, and thrusting and stabbing; after more than a year they had all become elite troops.

sentences.zh: 六年，召至闕，辭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was summoned to the capital and declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he was summoned to the capital and declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 出知靜江府兼廣西經略安撫使，又辭。

translations.literal: He was sent out to govern Ching-chiang Prefecture, concurrently Kwangsi Military Commissioner and Pacification Commissioner, and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Ching-chiang and concurrent Kwangsi Military Commissioner and Pacification Commissioner, but again declined.

sentences.zh: 權廣西運判兼提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He served concurrently as acting Kwangsi transport intendant and judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the concurrent posts of acting Kwangsi transport intendant and judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 宰相移書槐曰：「國家方用兵，人臣不辭急難，公幸毋固辭。」

translations.literal: The chief councilor sent a letter to Huai saying: "The state is currently at war; a subject must not shrink from urgent difficulties—Sir, please do not stubbornly decline."
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor wrote to Huai, saying, "The state is currently at war; a subject must not shrink from urgent difficulties—please do not stubbornly decline, sir."

sentences.zh: 槐即日就道，至邕州，上守禦七策。

translations.literal: That same day Huai set out on the road; arriving at Yung Prefecture, he submitted seven strategies for defense.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Huai set out on the road; upon reaching Yung Prefecture, he submitted seven strategies for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 邕州之地西通諸蠻夷，南引交址及符奴、月烏、流鱗之屬，數寇邊，槐與約無相侵，推赤心遇之，皆伏不動。

translations.literal: The territory of Yung Prefecture westward connects with various Man and Yi peoples; southward it adjoins Chiao-chih and groups such as Fu-nu, Yüeh-wu, and Liu-lin, who repeatedly raided the frontier. Huai made pacts with them not to invade one another, treated them with open heart, and they all submitted and did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Yung Prefecture bordered various tribal peoples to the west and, to the south, Chiao-chih and groups such as Fu-nu, Yüeh-wu, and Liu-lin, who repeatedly raided the frontier. Huai made non-aggression pacts with them and treated them with sincerity, and they all submitted and remained quiet.

sentences.zh: 又與交址約五事：一無犯邊，二歸我侵地，三還鹵掠生口，四奉正朔，五通貿易。

translations.literal: He also agreed with Chiao-chih on five points: first, not to violate the frontier; second, to return our invaded territory; third, to return captives taken by raiding; fourth, to observe our calendar; fifth, to conduct trade.
translations.idiomatic: He also concluded a five-point agreement with Chiao-chih: no frontier violations, return of invaded territory, return of captives taken in raids, observance of the Sung calendar, and open trade.

sentences.zh: 於是遣使來獻方物、大象南方悉定。

translations.literal: Thereupon they sent envoys to present tribute goods and elephants, and the entire south was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were then dispatched bearing tribute goods and elephants, and the entire south was pacified.

sentences.zh: 七年，進寶章閣待制。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was advanced to gentlemen-at-attendance in the Pao-chang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, he was promoted to gentlemen-at-attendance in the Pao-chang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷工部侍郎，職事依舊，兼轉運使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works; his duties remained as before, concurrently transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works while retaining his previous duties, concurrently serving as transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九年，召赴闕，封定遠縣男。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was summoned to the capital and enfeoffed as Baron of Ting-yuan County.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, he was summoned to court and enfeoffed as Baron of Ting-yuan County.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部侍郎兼權給事中兼侍讀，升給事中，上疏請抑損戚裏恩澤以慰天下士大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War, concurrently acting Supervising Censor and Court Reader; he was promoted to Supervising Censor and submitted a memorial asking to curtail the favors granted to imperial consort clans in order to reassure scholars and officials throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of War, concurrently acting supervising censor and court reader, then promoted supervising censor; he submitted a memorial asking that favors granted to imperial consort clans be curtailed so as to reassure scholars and officials throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 群臣奏事少與法違，憚槐不敢上。

translations.literal: When officials presented affairs that in small ways violated the law, they feared Huai and did not dare submit them.
translations.idiomatic: When officials had business that in some measure violated the law, they feared Huai and dared not submit it.

sentences.zh: 兼侍讀，進寶章閣直學士、知福州福建安撫使，辭。

translations.literal: Concurrently Court Reader, he was advanced to academician in the Pao-chang Pavilion, appointed prefect of Fu-chou and Fukien Pacification Commissioner, and declined.
translations.idiomatic: As concurrent court reader he was promoted to academician in the Pao-chang Pavilion and appointed prefect of Fu-chou and Fukien pacification commissioner, but declined.

sentences.zh: 進封子。

translations.literal: His son was advanced in enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son was promoted in rank of enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事，進封侯。

translations.literal: That winter he was appointed academician of the Tuan-ming Hall and co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and advanced in enfeoffment to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed academician of the Tuan-ming Hall and co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and elevated in enfeoffment to marquis.

sentences.zh: 十二年，為同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he served as co-director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, he became co-director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 寶祐元年，權參知政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Pao-yu, he served as acting Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Pao-yu, he served as acting associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 二年，進參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was advanced to Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he was promoted to associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 四川制置使餘晦以戰敗奪官，詔荊襄制置使李曾伯往視師，曾伯辭，槐曰：「事如此，尚可坐而睨乎？」

translations.literal: The Szechwan frontier commissioner Yü Hui was stripped of office for defeat in battle; the throne ordered the Ching-Hsiang frontier commissioner Li Tseng-po to go inspect the armies. Tseng-po declined. Huai said: "Matters being thus, how can one still sit and look on indifferently?"
translations.idiomatic: The Szechwan frontier commissioner Yü Hui was stripped of office for defeat in battle; the throne ordered the Ching-Hsiang frontier commissioner Li Tseng-po to go inspect the armies, but Tseng-po declined. Huai said, "Matters being thus, how can one still sit back and watch indifferently?"

sentences.zh: 上疏請行，頓重兵夔門以固荊、蜀輔車之勢，詔報曰：「腹心之臣，所與共理天下者也，宜在朝廷，不宜在四方。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting to go himself, massing heavy troops at K'uei Gate to solidify the mutually supporting positions of Ching and Shu. The edict in reply said: "A trusted minister is one who jointly governs the realm with Us; he ought to be at court, not in the four directions."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial asking to go in person and concentrate heavy troops at K'uei Gate to strengthen the mutual support between Ching and Shu. The edict replied, "A trusted minister is one who jointly governs the realm with Us; he ought to remain at court, not be sent to the four quarters."

sentences.zh: 復上疏曰：「天下之事，不進則退，人臣無敢為岐意者，苟以臣為可任，宜少聽臣自效，即臣不足與軍旅之事，願上官爵。」

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial saying: "Affairs under Heaven advance or retreat—there is no middle way; no subject dares entertain divergent intent. If Your Majesty deems me fit to be entrusted, please grant me some latitude to prove myself; if I am inadequate for military affairs, I ask to be relieved of rank and office."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial, saying, "Affairs under Heaven either advance or retreat—there is no standing still—and no subject dares entertain divergent intent. If Your Majesty deems me fit for trust, please grant me some latitude to prove myself; if I am inadequate for military affairs, I beg to be relieved of rank and office."

sentences.zh: 不許，進封濠梁郡公。

translations.literal: This was not granted; he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Hao-liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His request was denied, and he was promoted in enfeoffment to Duke of Hao-liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝日鄉用槐，槐言事無所隱，意在於格君心之非而不為容悅。

translations.literal: The emperor increasingly employed Huai; Huai spoke on affairs without concealment, intending to correct what was wrong in the ruler's mind and not to offer pleasing flattery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relied on Huai more and more; Huai spoke frankly on affairs, intending to correct what was wrong in the ruler's mind rather than offer pleasing flattery.

sentences.zh: 帝問糴民粟積邊，則對曰：「吳民困甚，有司急糴不復省。

translations.literal: When the emperor asked about purchasing the people's grain to store on the frontier, he replied: "The people of Wu are greatly distressed; the officials urgently purchase grain without further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked about purchasing civilian grain to stock the frontier, he replied, "The people of Wu are greatly distressed; officials urgently requisition grain without regard for their plight.

sentences.zh: 夫民惟邦本，願先垂意根本。」

translations.literal: The people are the foundation of the state; I wish Your Majesty would first attend to the root."
translations.idiomatic: The people are the foundation of the state; I wish Your Majesty would first attend to that root."

sentences.zh: 帝問修太乙祠，則對曰：「土工薦起，民罷于徵發，非所以事天也。」

translations.literal: When the emperor asked about repairing the Grand Unity Shrine, he replied: "Earthworks pile up layer upon layer; the people are wearied by levies of labor—this is not the way to serve Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked about repairing the Grand Unity Shrine, he replied, "Earthworks rise layer upon layer and the people are exhausted by conscript labor—this is not the way to serve Heaven."

sentences.zh: 帝問邊事，對曰：「外有敵國，則其計先自強。

translations.literal: When the emperor asked about frontier affairs, he replied: "With enemy states abroad, one's first plan should be self-strengthening.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked about frontier affairs, he replied, "With enemy states abroad, one's first plan must be self-strengthening.

sentences.zh: 自強者人畏我，我不畏人。」

translations.literal: Those who strengthen themselves make others fear them; they do not fear others."
translations.idiomatic: Those who strengthen themselves are feared by others; they need not fear others."

sentences.zh: 又言：「敵國在前，宜拔材能用之。

translations.literal: He further said: "With enemy states before us, talented men ought to be selected and employed.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "With enemy states before us, talented men ought to be selected and put to use.

sentences.zh: 士大夫有過失，為執法吏所刺劾，終身擯弗用，深為朝廷惜此。

translations.literal: When scholar-officials had faults and were impeached by law-enforcement officers, they were excluded and never employed for life—the court deeply regretted this waste.
translations.idiomatic: When scholar-officials had faults and were impeached by law-enforcement officers, they were barred from employment for life—the court deeply regretted this waste of talent.

sentences.zh: 苟非奸邪，皆願為昭洗，勿廢其他善。

translations.literal: If they were not treacherous and wicked, I wish all would be cleared and rehabilitated and their other merits not discarded.
translations.idiomatic: If they were not treacherous and wicked, I wish that all would be cleared and rehabilitated, and their other merits not discarded.

sentences.zh: 又遷謫之臣，久墮遐方，稍稍內徙，今得生還，顧弗用可矣。」

translations.literal: Also, exiled and demoted officials who had long fallen into distant regions and were gradually moved inward—now having returned alive, it would be enough merely not to employ them."
translations.idiomatic: As for exiled and demoted officials who had long languished in distant regions and were gradually moved inland—now that they have returned alive, it would suffice merely not to employ them."

sentences.zh: 槐每奏，帝輒稱善。

translations.literal: Whenever Huai memorialized, the emperor always praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Huai memorialized, the emperor always praised him.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜右丞相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed Right Grand Councilor and concurrently Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, he was appointed Right Grand Councilor and concurrently director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 槐自以為人主所振拔，苟可以利安國家無不為，然務先大體，任人先取故舊之在疏遠者，在官者率滿歲而遷。

translations.literal: Huai, considering himself raised up by the ruler, did whatever could benefit and settle the state; yet he attended first to the larger pattern, selecting for appointment first old associates who were in remote posts, and those in office generally transferred after a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Huai, considering himself elevated by the sovereign, did whatever could benefit the state; yet he attended first to the larger pattern, appointing first old associates in remote posts, and generally rotating those in office after a full year.

sentences.zh: 嗜進者始不說矣。

translations.literal: Those greedy for advancement at first were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Those greedy for advancement were displeased at first.

sentences.zh: 槐又言於帝曰：「臣為政而有害政者三。」

translations.literal: Huai also said to the emperor: "In my administration there are three things that harm governance."
translations.idiomatic: Huai also told the emperor, "In my administration there are three things that harm governance."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「胡為害政者三？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What are the three things that harm governance?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What are the three things that harm governance?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「戚里不奉法，一矣；

translations.literal: He replied: "Imperial consort clans do not observe the law—that is the first;
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Imperial consort clans do not observe the law—that is the first;

sentences.zh: 執法大吏久於其官而擅威福，二矣；

translations.literal: senior law-enforcement officials long in their posts and arrogating authority and favor—that is the second;
translations.idiomatic: senior law-enforcement officials who remain long in their posts and arrogated authority and favor—that is the second;

sentences.zh: 皇城司不檢士，三矣。

translations.literal: the Palace Command does not restrain its soldiers—that is the third.
translations.idiomatic: the Palace Command does not restrain its soldiers—that is the third.

sentences.zh: 將率不檢下故士卒橫，士卒橫則變生於無時；

translations.literal: Generals do not restrain their subordinates, hence soldiers are unruly; when soldiers are unruly, mutiny may arise at any time;
translations.idiomatic: Generals fail to restrain their subordinates, so soldiers run riot; when soldiers run riot, mutiny may arise at any time;

sentences.zh: 執法威福擅故賢不肖混淆，賢不肖混淆則奸邪肆，賢人伏而不出；

translations.literal: law-enforcement officials arrogating authority and favor cause the worthy and unworthy to be confused; when the worthy and unworthy are confused, the wicked run rampant and the worthy hide and do not emerge;
translations.idiomatic: when law-enforcement officials arrogating authority and favor blur the distinction between the worthy and unworthy, the wicked run rampant while the worthy hide and do not emerge;

sentences.zh: 親戚不奉法故法令輕，法令輕故朝廷卑。

translations.literal: when kinsmen do not observe the law, therefore the laws are lightly regarded; when the laws are lightly regarded, therefore the court is held in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: when kinsmen do not observe the law, statutes lose weight; when statutes lose weight, the court is held in contempt.

sentences.zh: 三者弗去，政且廢，願自上除之。」

translations.literal: If these three are not removed, governance will be ruined; I wish Your Majesty would eliminate them from above."
translations.idiomatic: If these three are not removed, governance will collapse; I beg Your Majesty to eliminate them from above."

sentences.zh: 於是嫉之者滋甚。

translations.literal: Thereupon those who envied him grew all the more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon those who envied him grew all the more numerous.

sentences.zh: 帝年浸高，操柄獨斷，群臣無當意者，漸喜狎佞人。

translations.literal: As the emperor's years gradually advanced, he wielded power alone and decided alone; no minister pleased him, and he gradually came to delight in consorting with flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor grew older, he wielded power alone; no minister pleased him, and he gradually came to delight in consorting with flatterers.

sentences.zh: 丁大全善為佞，帝躐貴之，竊弄威權而帝弗覺悟。

translations.literal: Ting Ta-chüan was skilled at flattery; the emperor skipped ranks to honor him, and he secretly manipulated authority and power while the emperor did not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: Ting Ta-chüan was skilled at flattery; the emperor promoted him by leaps and bounds, and he secretly wielded authority while the emperor remained unaware.

sentences.zh: 大全已為侍御史，遣客私自結於槐，槐曰：「吾聞人臣無私交，吾惟事上，不敢私結約，幸為謝丁君。」

translations.literal: Ta-chüan was already an attending censor and sent a client to seek a private connection with Huai. Huai said: "I have heard that ministers have no private associations; I serve only the ruler and dare not make private pacts—please convey my thanks to Master Ting."
translations.idiomatic: Ta-chüan was already an attending censor and sent an agent to seek a private connection with Huai. Huai said, "I have heard that ministers must have no private associations; I serve only the ruler and dare not make private pacts—please convey my thanks to Master Ting."

sentences.zh: 大全度槐弗善己，銜甚，乃日夜刻求槐短。

translations.literal: Ta-chüan judged that Huai did not favor him and resented him deeply; day and night he sought out Huai's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Ta-chüan concluded that Huai did not favor him and deeply resented him; day and night he sought out Huai's faults.

sentences.zh: 槐入見，極言大全邪佞不可近。

translations.literal: When Huai entered audience, he spoke at length that Ta-chüan was a wicked flatterer and must not be approached.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai entered audience, he spoke at length that Ta-chüan was a wicked flatterer and must not be approached.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「大全未嘗短卿，卿勿疑。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ta-chüan has never spoken ill of you—do not suspect him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Ta-chüan has never spoken ill of you—do not suspect him."

sentences.zh: 槐曰：「臣與大全何怨？

translations.literal: Huai said: "What grudge do I have with Ta-chüan?
translations.idiomatic: Huai said, "What grudge do I have with Ta-chüan?

sentences.zh: 顧陛下拔臣至此，臣知大全邪而噤不言，是負陛下也。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty raised me to this position; if I know Ta-chüan is wicked and keep silent, that is failing Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty raised me to this position; if I know Ta-chüan is wicked and keep silent, I would be failing Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 且陛下謂大全忠而臣以為奸，不可與俱事陛下矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty deems Ta-chüan loyal while I deem him treacherous—we cannot both serve Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty deems Ta-chüan loyal while I deem him treacherous—we cannot both continue to serve Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 既罷出，即上書乞骸骨，不報。

translations.literal: When the audience ended he immediately submitted a memorial requesting retirement; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: When the audience ended he immediately submitted a memorial requesting retirement; there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 四年，策免丞相，以觀文殿大學士提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was dismissed as grand councilor by imperial rescript and appointed Grand Academician of the Kuan-wen Hall to direct the Tung-hsiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was dismissed as grand councilor by imperial rescript and appointed Grand Academician of the Kuan-wen Hall to direct the Tung-hsiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 時大全亦論劾槐，書未下，自發省兵迫遣之。

translations.literal: At that time Ta-chüan also impeached Huai; before the memorial was issued, he himself dispatched provincial troops to force Huai to depart.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ta-chüan also impeached Huai; before the memorial was issued, he himself dispatched provincial troops to force Huai to depart.

sentences.zh: 於是太學諸生陳宜中等上書爭之，語見《大全傳》。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Imperial College students Ch'en I-chung and others submitted memorials protesting; the account appears in the biography of Ta-chüan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Imperial College students including Ch'en I-chung submitted memorials in protest; the account appears in the biography of Ta-chüan.

sentences.zh: 五年及景定元年，俱用祀明堂恩加食邑。

translations.literal: In the fifth year and in the first year of Ching-ting, both times he received increased fief income through the Bright Hall sacrifice grace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year and in the first year of Ching-ting, he received increased fief income on both occasions through the Bright Hall sacrifice grace.

sentences.zh: 二年，特授判福州、福建路安撫大使，固辭。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was specially appointed judge of Fu-chou and Great Pacification Commissioner of the Fukien Circuit, and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he was specially appointed judge of Fu-chou and Great Pacification Commissioner of the Fukien Circuit, but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 進封吉國，又進封許國公。

translations.literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Chi State, and again advanced to Duke of Hsü State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in enfeoffment to Duke of Chi State, and again promoted to Duke of Hsü State.

sentences.zh: 三年五月二十八日既夕，天大雨，烈風雷電，槐起衣冠而坐，麾婦人出，為諸生說《兌》、《謙》二卦，問夜如何？

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month in the third year, at dusk, heaven sent down great rain, fierce wind, thunder, and lightning; Huai rose, put on cap and robes, and sat; he ordered the women out, lectured his students on the K'ui and Ch'ien hexagrams, and asked what hour of the night it was.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month in the third year, at dusk, heaven sent down torrential rain, fierce wind, thunder, and lightning; Huai rose, dressed in cap and robes, and sat upright; he ordered the women out, lectured his students on the K'ui and Ch'ien hexagrams, and asked what hour of the night it was.

sentences.zh: 諸生以夜中對，遂薨。

translations.literal: The students answered that it was midnight, and thereupon he died.
translations.idiomatic: The students answered that it was midnight, and thereupon he died.

sentences.zh: 遺表上，贈太子少師，諡文清。

translations.literal: When his final memorial was submitted, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wen-ch'ing.
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial was submitted, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wen-ch'ing.

sentences.zh: 帝使使致金六十斤、帛千匹以賻。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to present sixty catties of gold and a thousand bolts of silk as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to present sixty catties of gold and a thousand bolts of silk as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 葉夢鼎

translations.literal: Yeh Meng-ting
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mengding

sentences.zh: 葉夢鼎，字鎮之，台之寧海人。

translations.literal: Yeh Meng-ting, styled Chên-chih, was a native of Ning-hai in T'ai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mengding, whose style was Chen-chih, was a native of Ning-hai in T'ai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本陳待聘之子，七歲後於母族。

translations.literal: Originally he was the son of Ch'en T'ai-p'in; at age seven he was given to his mother's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Originally he was the son of Ch'en T'ai-p'in; at age seven he was given to his mother's clan.

sentences.zh: 少從直龍圖閣鄭霖、宗正少卿趙逢龍學，以太學上舍試入優等，兩優釋褐出身，授信州軍事推官，攝教事，講荒政。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Cheng Lin, associate in the Chih Lung-t'u Pavilion, and Chao Feng-lung, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court; through the Superior Imperial College examination he entered with highest distinction, and with two highest grades he received initial appointment, was appointed military judicial officer of Hsin Prefecture, acted as instructor, and lectured on famine administration.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Cheng Lin, associate in the Chih Lung-t'u Pavilion, and Chao Feng-lung, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court; through the Superior Imperial College examination he entered with highest distinction, and with two highest grades received initial appointment as military judicial officer of Hsin Prefecture, acted as instructor, and lectured on famine administration.

sentences.zh: 遷太學錄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Recorder of the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to recorder of the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 淳祐二年，雷變，上封事，言召人才，戒媟近。

translations.literal: In the second year of Ch'un-yu, when thunder changed its pattern, he submitted a sealed memorial urging the summoning of talent and warning against intimacy with the unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Ch'un-yu, when thunder changed its pattern, he submitted a sealed memorial urging the summoning of talent and warning against intimacy with the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 明年，輪對，言君子、直言、軍制、楮幣、任官、分閫六事。

translations.literal: The next year, in audience rotation, he spoke on six matters: the gentleman, forthright speech, military institutions, paper currency, appointment of officials, and division of frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in audience rotation, he spoke on six matters: the gentleman, forthright speech, military institutions, paper currency, appointment of officials, and division of frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 同番易湯巾召試館職，授秘書省正字。

translations.literal: In the same rotation as T'ang Chin he was summoned to examination for a palace post and appointed Corrector in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the same rotation as T'ang Chin he was summoned to examination for a palace post and appointed corrector in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，升校書郎兼莊文府教授。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was promoted to Proofreader, concurrently instructor in the Chuang-wen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was promoted to proofreader, concurrently instructor in the Chuang-wen Hall.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷秘書郎，轉對，言定國本，求哲輔，專閫帥，獎用介直。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was transferred to Secretariat Drafter; in audience rotation he spoke on establishing the heir, seeking wise assistants, assigning frontier commanders, and rewarding the upright and forthright.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he was transferred to secretariat drafter; in audience rotation he spoke on establishing the heir, seeking wise assistants, assigning frontier commanders, and rewarding the upright and forthright.

sentences.zh: 雷變上言，援唐康澄「五可畏」之說，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: When thunder changed its pattern he submitted a memorial citing T'ang K'ang-ch'eng's doctrine of the "five things to be feared," and was transferred to Assistant Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When thunder changed its pattern he submitted a memorial citing T'ang K'ang-ch'eng's doctrine of the "five things to be feared," and was transferred to assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜軍器少監兼兵部郎官，轉對，言國計、邊事、國體三事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed Vice Director of the Armory, concurrently bureau officer in the Ministry of War; in audience rotation he spoke on three matters: state finance, frontier affairs, and the integrity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he was appointed Vice Director of the Armory, concurrently bureau officer in the Ministry of War; in audience rotation he spoke on three matters: state finance, frontier affairs, and the integrity of the state.

sentences.zh: 又言：「外有窺邊之大敵，內有伺隙之巨奸；

translations.literal: He also said: "Abroad there is a great enemy watching the frontier; within there is a great villain watching for an opening;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Abroad there is a great enemy watching the frontier; within there is a great villain watching for an opening;

sentences.zh: 奇邪蠱媚于宮闈，熏腐依憑於城社；

translations.literal: strange and wicked persons beguile within the palace precincts, and corrupt minions lean on the state as on a city god;
translations.idiomatic: strange and wicked persons beguile within the palace precincts, and corrupt minions lean on the state as on a city god;

sentences.zh: 強藩悍將，牙蘖易搖，草竊奸宄，肘腋階變。」

translations.literal: powerful frontier lords and fierce generals sprout shoots easily shaken; grass-thieves and hidden evildoers may trigger sudden change at the elbow and armpit."
translations.idiomatic: powerful frontier lords and fierce generals sprout shoots easily shaken; grass-thieves and hidden evildoers may trigger sudden change at one's very side."

sentences.zh: 權知袁州，轉運司和糴米三萬斛，夢鼎言：「袁山多而田少，朝廷免和糴已百年，自今開之，百姓子孫受無窮之害，則無窮之怨從之。」

translations.literal: Acting as prefect of Yüan Prefecture, the transport commission arranged to purchase thirty thousand hu of rice; Meng-ting said: "Yüan has many mountains and little farmland; the court exempted coordinated purchase for a hundred years already; if it is opened now, the people's descendants will suffer endless harm, and endless resentment will follow."
translations.idiomatic: Acting as prefect of Yüan Prefecture, the transport commission arranged to purchase thirty thousand hu of rice; Meng-ting said, "Yüan has many mountains and little farmland; the court exempted coordinated purchase there for a hundred years already; if it is opened now, the people's descendants will suffer endless harm, and endless resentment will follow."

sentences.zh: 民湯頎獻田學官，妻子離散，夢鼎遂還之。
