translations.literal: A commoner named T'ang K'ai offered land to the school official; his wife and children were scattered in separation—Meng-ting returned the land to him.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named T'ang K'ai offered land to the school official; his wife and children were scattered in separation—Meng-ting returned the land to him.

sentences.zh: 毀萬載旗𥮉村淫祠，塞其妖井。

translations.literal: He destroyed the licentious shrine at Ch'i-ch'i Village in Wan-tsai and blocked up its demon well.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed the licentious shrine at Ch'i-ch'i Village in Wan-tsai and blocked up its demon well.

sentences.zh: 召赴行在。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 丁本生母憂。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: He observed mourning for his birth mother.

sentences.zh: 十一年，免喪，拜司封員外郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when mourning ended, he was appointed Outer Department Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when mourning ended, he was appointed Outer Department vice director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 輪對，言：「陛下惑于左右之讒說，例視言者為好名，中傷既深，膠固莫解。

translations.literal: In audience rotation he said: "Your Majesty is deluded by slander from those at your side and routinely treats those who speak as seekers of fame; slander has cut deep, and obstinacy cannot be dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: In audience rotation he said, "Your Majesty is deluded by slander from those at your side and routinely treats those who speak as seekers of fame; slander has cut deep, and obstinacy cannot be dissolved.

sentences.zh: 近歲以來，言稍犯人主之所難者，不顯罷則陰黜，不久外則設間，去者屢召而不還，來者一鳴而輒斥。」

translations.literal: In recent years, when speech in small measure touched what the ruler finds difficult, if not openly dismissed then secretly demoted; if not soon sent out then traps were set; those who left were repeatedly summoned but not returned, and those who came were expelled at the first outcry."
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, when speech in some measure touched what the ruler finds difficult, if not openly dismissed then secretly demoted; if not soon sent out then traps were set; those who left were repeatedly summoned but not returned, and those who came were expelled at the first outcry."

sentences.zh: 兼玉牒檢討官，以直秘閣、江西提舉常平兼知吉州。

translations.literal: Concurrently Compiler of the Imperial Genealogy, he was appointed associate in the Chih Secret Archive, Kiangsi Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries, concurrently prefect of Chi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrently compiler of the Imperial Genealogy, he was appointed associate in the Chih Secret Archive, Kiangsi intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries, concurrently prefect of Chi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 節制悍將，置社倉、義倉，平反李義山受贓之冤，以國子司業召。

translations.literal: He restrained fierce generals, established community granaries and charity granaries, cleared Li I-shan's false conviction for accepting bribes, and was summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He kept fierce generals under control, established community and charity granaries, cleared Li I-shan's false conviction for bribery, and was summoned to serve as vice director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 寶祐元年陛對，言國論主平江西義倉，不可待申省而後發。

translations.literal: In the first year of Pao-yu, at imperial audience he spoke on state policy, holding that Kiangsi charity granaries should be opened without waiting for provincial report.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Pao-yu, in audience with the emperor he argued that Kiangsi's charity granaries should be opened at once and must not wait for a provincial report.

sentences.zh: 考試集英殿，授崇政殿說書，進講《尚書》。

translations.literal: Examined at the Hall of Assembled Excellence, he was appointed lecturer at the Hall of Venerated Governance and advanced to lecture on the Book of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: After examination in the Hall of Assembled Excellence, he was appointed lecturer at the Hall of Venerated Governance and began lecturing on the Book of Documents.

sentences.zh: 兼國史編修、實錄檢討，遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Concurrently Compiler of the National History and Examiner of the Veritable Records, he was transferred to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrently compiler of the National History and examiner of the Veritable Records, he was transferred to chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼權禮部侍郎，諫幸西太乙宮。

translations.literal: In the second year, concurrently Acting Vice Minister of Rites, he remonstrated against an imperial visit to the Western T'ai-i Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, while also serving as acting vice minister of Rites, he remonstrated against the emperor's planned visit to the Western T'ai-i Palace.

sentences.zh: 三年，權禮部侍郎，仍兼祭酒，升兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰，尋兼侍講。

translations.literal: In the third year, as Acting Vice Minister of Rites he still concurrently served as Chancellor, was promoted to concurrently Co-Compiler of the National History and Co-Compiler of the Veritable Records Academy, and soon additionally served as Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he remained acting vice minister of Rites and chancellor, was promoted to co-compiler of the National History and co-compiler of the Veritable Records Academy, and soon added the post of court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 五年，以集英殿修撰差知贛州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, as Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Excellence he was assigned to govern Kan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, as a compiler at the Hall of Assembled Excellence, he was assigned to govern Kan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁大全柄國，欲挽夢鼎登朝，卒辭謝之。

translations.literal: Ting Ta-ch'üan held state power and wished to draw Meng-ting to court; in the end Meng-ting declined and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Ting Ta-ch'üan dominated the government and tried to bring Meng-ting into court service, but Meng-ting ultimately declined.

sentences.zh: 六年，改知建寧府，又改知隆興府。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was transferred to govern Chien-ning Prefecture, then again transferred to govern Lung-hsing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Chien-ning Prefecture, and then to Lung-hsing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開慶元年，復知建寧府，作橋樑，置驛舍，建大安關，決疑獄。

translations.literal: In the first year of K'ai-ch'ing, he again governed Chien-ning Prefecture, built bridges, established post stations, built the Ta-an Pass, and decided doubtful legal cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of K'ai-ch'ing he again governed Chien-ning Prefecture, built bridges and post stations, constructed the Ta-an Pass, and resolved doubtful criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 景定元年，召為太子詹事，上疏以「法天」為言。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ching-ting, he was summoned as Tutor to the Crown Prince and submitted a memorial speaking on "aligning with Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ching-ting he was summoned to serve as tutor to the crown prince and submitted a memorial on aligning the throne with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，賜甯海縣食邑。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and granted the food fief of Ning-hai County.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of Personnel and granted the food fief of Ning-hai County.

sentences.zh: 二年，權兵部尚書兼權吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year, he served as Acting Minister of War concurrently with Acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he served concurrently as acting minister of War and acting minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷兵部尚書兼修國史兼實錄修撰。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to Minister of War, concurrently Compiler of the National History and Compiler of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to minister of War, while also serving as compiler of the National History and compiler of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，五辭免，請祠，不允。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel, declined dismissal five times, requested a sinecure post, and was not granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of Personnel, declined the appointment five times and asked for a sinecure post, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 拜端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事，屢辭不許。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Tuan-ming Hall and Co-Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he repeatedly declined and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed academician of the Tuan-ming Hall and co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but repeatedly declined and was not allowed to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 同提舉編修《經武要略》兼太子賓客，進封甯海伯。

translations.literal: Concurrently Director of the compilation of the Essential Military Compendium and Guest of the Crown Prince, he was advanced in rank to Marquis of Ning-hai.
translations.idiomatic: As co-director of the compilation of the Essential Military Compendium and guest of the crown prince, he was advanced to marquis of Ning-hai.

sentences.zh: 四年，簽書樞密院事，進封臨海郡侯，以明堂恩進封臨海郡公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, as Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs he was advanced to Marquis of Lin-hai Commandery, and by Bright Hall grace was advanced to Duke of Lin-hai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, as signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs he was made marquis of Lin-hai Commandery, and by Bright Hall grace was further enfeoffed as duke of Lin-hai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 丞相賈似道欲造關子，罷十七、十八兩界會子，夢鼎以為厲民，乃止罷十七界。

translations.literal: Chancellor Chia Ssu-tao wished to create kuan-tzu notes and abolish the seventeenth and eighteenth series hui-tzu notes; Meng-ting thought it would harm the people, so only the seventeenth series was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Chia Ssu-tao wanted to issue kuan-tzu notes and abolish both the seventeenth and eighteenth series of hui-tzu notes; Meng-ting argued that this would harm the people, so only the seventeenth series was abolished.

sentences.zh: 公田法行，夢鼎又以為厲民，故行之浙右而止。

translations.literal: When the public-field law was implemented, Meng-ting again thought it would harm the people, so it was applied only in Che-chiang west and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the public-field law was put into effect, Meng-ting again held that it would burden the people, so the policy was carried out only in western Che-chiang and no farther.

sentences.zh: 五年，三辭，不許，進同知樞密院事、權參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he declined three times and was not permitted; he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Acting Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he declined three times without success and was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 以彗星出，夢鼎言政上下恐懼交修之日，乞解機政，又不許。

translations.literal: Because a comet appeared, Meng-ting said it was a day when ruler and subjects should jointly repair governance in fear; he requested release from state affairs and was again not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared, Meng-ting said it was a time for ruler and subjects alike to reform government in fear; he asked to be relieved of state duties, but again was refused.

sentences.zh: 奏免浙西經界。

translations.literal: He memorialized to abolish the land survey in Che-chiang west.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial calling for the abolition of the land survey in western Che-chiang.

sentences.zh: 理宗崩，議太子即位，太后垂簾聽政，夢鼎曰：「母后垂簾，豈是美事！」

translations.literal: When Emperor Li-tsung died, they deliberated on the crown prince's accession and the empress dowager holding court behind a curtain; Meng-ting said: "The empress dowager holding the curtain—how is that a fine thing!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Li-tsung died, the court debated the crown prince's accession and the empress dowager's regency from behind the curtain; Meng-ting said, "An empress dowager holding court behind a curtain—is that really something to welcome?"

sentences.zh: 進參知政事，加食邑。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Councilor and his food fief was increased.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand councilor and granted an increase in his food fief.

sentences.zh: 夢鼎力辭，似道懇留之，不可。

translations.literal: Meng-ting forcefully declined; Ssu-tao earnestly detained him, but could not keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng-ting forcefully declined the post; Ssu-tao earnestly pressed him to stay, but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 帝勉諭再三，詔閣門封還奏疏。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly exhorted him, and an edict ordered the Gate of the Inner Court to seal and return his memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly urged him to remain, and an edict ordered the Gate of the Inner Court to seal and return his memorials of resignation.

sentences.zh: 似道奏：「參政去則江萬里、王爚必不來」理宗復土，攝少傅，竣事，引疾歸裏，累詔，力辭，授資政殿學士、知慶元府、沿海制置使。

translations.literal: Ssu-tao memorialized: "If the Grand Councilor leaves, then Chiang Wan-li and Wang Yao will surely not come." At Emperor Li-tsung's re-burial he acted as Junior Tutor; when the rite was complete he cited illness and returned home; repeatedly summoned by edict, he forcefully declined and was appointed Academician of the Tzu-cheng Hall, prefect of Ch'ing-yüan, and Coastal Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Ssu-tao memorialized, "If the grand councilor leaves, Chiang Wan-li and Wang Yao will surely not come." At Emperor Li-tsung's re-burial Meng-ting served as acting junior tutor; when the rites were finished he pleaded illness and returned home. Though repeatedly summoned by edict, he forcefully declined and was appointed academician of the Tzu-cheng Hall, prefect of Ch'ing-yüan, and coastal pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 肅清海寇，罪止首惡，羨余之費，悉卻不受。

translations.literal: He cleared away sea bandits, punished only the ringleaders, and entirely refused all surplus expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed sea bandits, limiting punishment to the ringleaders, and refused every surplus fee offered to him.

sentences.zh: 建濟民倉以備饑歲，造驛舍以待賓旅。

translations.literal: He built relief granaries against famine years and constructed post stations to receive traveling guests.
translations.idiomatic: He built relief granaries to guard against famine and constructed post stations for traveling guests.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳三年，再召為參知政事，加食邑，六辭，不許。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hsien-ch'un, he was again summoned as Grand Councilor, his food fief was increased, he declined six times, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hsien-ch'un he was again summoned as grand councilor and granted an increase in his food fief; he declined six times, but was not allowed to refuse.

sentences.zh: 詔著作佐郎盧鉞與台州守項公采趣行，拜特進、右丞相兼樞密使，累辭，不許，乃與似道分任。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Assistant Compiler Lu Yüeh and T'ai-chou prefect Hsiang Kung-ts'ai to urge him to proceed; he was appointed Specially Advanced, Right Chancellor concurrently Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he repeatedly declined and was not permitted, and then shared duties with Ssu-tao.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Assistant Compiler Lu Yüeh and the prefect of T'ai-chou, Hsiang Kung-ts'ai, to hurry him to court; he was appointed specially advanced, right chancellor, and director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. He declined repeatedly without success and then shared duties with Ssu-tao.

sentences.zh: 利州轉運使王價嘗以言去官，非其罪也，四川制置司已辟參議，及死，其子訴求遺澤。

translations.literal: Li-chou Transport Commissioner Wang Chia had once left office for his words, not for his crime; the Szechwan Pacification Commission had already appointed him deliberating officer, and when he died his son petitioned seeking posthumous favors.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chia, transport commissioner of Li-chou, had once lost office for something he said, not for any crime; the Szechwan pacification commission had already appointed him as deliberating officer, and after his death his son petitioned for posthumous favors.

sentences.zh: 至是，夢鼎明其無罪，似道以為恩不己出，罷省部吏數人，榜其姓名於朝。

translations.literal: At this time Meng-ting clarified his innocence; Ssu-tao thought the favor did not originate from himself, dismissed several provincial and ministry clerks, and posted their names at court.
translations.idiomatic: Meng-ting now cleared Wang of wrongdoing; Ssu-tao, believing the favor had not come from himself, dismissed several provincial and ministry clerks and posted their names at court.

sentences.zh: 夢鼎怒曰：「我斷不為陳自強。」

translations.literal: Meng-ting angrily said: "I will absolutely not be like Ch'en Tzu-ch'iang."
translations.idiomatic: Meng-ting said in anger, "I will never behave like Ch'en Tzu-ch'iang."

sentences.zh: 即求去。

translations.literal: He immediately requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 似道之母讓似道曰：「葉丞相安于家食，未嘗希進，汝強與以相印，今乃牽制至此，若不從吾言，吾不食矣。」

translations.literal: Ssu-tao's mother reproached Ssu-tao, saying: "Chancellor Yeh is content with home fare and never coveted advancement; you forcibly gave him the chancellor's seal, and now he is constrained to this point; if you do not follow my words, I will not eat."
translations.idiomatic: Ssu-tao's mother rebuked him, saying, "Chancellor Yeh was content at home and never sought advancement; you forced the chancellor's seal on him, and now matters have come to this pass. If you do not do as I say, I will stop eating."

sentences.zh: 似道曰：「為官不得不如此。」

translations.literal: Ssu-tao said: "In office one cannot help being thus."
translations.idiomatic: Ssu-tao replied, "In office one cannot always avoid acting this way."

sentences.zh: 會太學諸生亦上書言似道專權固位，乃悔悟，屬府尹洪燾求解，而夢鼎屢上章乞閑。

translations.literal: Just then National University students also submitted memorials saying Ssu-tao monopolized power and clung to office; he then repented, entrusted Capital Intendant Hung Tao to seek reconciliation, while Meng-ting repeatedly submitted memorials requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time students of the National University also submitted memorials accusing Ssu-tao of monopolizing power and clinging to office. He then repented and asked the capital intendant Hung Tao to mediate, while Meng-ting repeatedly submitted memorials asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 冬雷，引咎求去愈力。

translations.literal: When winter thunder occurred, he took blame and sought dismissal with greater force.
translations.idiomatic: After winter thunder appeared, he took the blame upon himself and pressed his resignation all the more forcefully.

sentences.zh: 四年，策楊妃，宰相無拜禮，吏贊拜，夢鼎以笏揮之，趨出。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, at the examination of Yang Fei, the chancellor had no bowing rite but clerks announced bowing; Meng-ting waved his tablet at them and hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, at the examination for Yang Fei, the chancellor was not to perform the bowing rite, yet clerks called for bows; Meng-ting waved his tablet at them and hurried out.

sentences.zh: 明日，乞還田裏，詔勉留之。

translations.literal: The next day he requested return to his fields; an edict urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he asked to return to his fields, but an edict urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 詔免諸州守臣上殿奏事，夢鼎言：「祖宗謹重牧守之寄，將赴官，必令奏事，蓋欲察其人品，及面諭以廉律己，愛育百姓。

translations.literal: An edict exempted prefectural governors from ascending the hall to report; Meng-ting said: "The ancestors carefully valued the commission of frontier governors; when about to take office they were always ordered to report, intending to observe their character and face-to-face instruct them to restrain themselves with integrity and cherish the people.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict exempted prefectural governors from ascending the hall to report, Meng-ting said, "The founders of the dynasty carefully valued the trust placed in frontier governors. Before taking office they were always required to report in person, so that the court could observe their character and instruct them face to face to govern with integrity and care for the people.

sentences.zh: 其至郡延見吏民，具宣上意，庶幾求無負臨遣之意。

translations.literal: On reaching their command they would receive officials and people and fully proclaim the emperor's intent, so that they might not betray the meaning of being sent forth.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching their posts they would receive officials and commoners and fully convey the emperor's intent, so that they would not fail the purpose for which they had been dispatched.

sentences.zh: 今不遠數千里而來，咫尺天顏而不得見，甚非立法之本意。」

translations.literal: Now, coming from thousands of li and not obtaining sight of the imperial countenance at arm's length—this greatly departs from the original intent of the law."
translations.idiomatic: Now men travel thousands of li and yet cannot see the emperor's face though he is within reach—this is far from the original intent of the institution."

sentences.zh: 又乞容受直言。

translations.literal: He also requested that forthright speech be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that forthright speech be welcomed.

sentences.zh: 進少保。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to junior guardian.

sentences.zh: 五年，引杜衍致仕單車宵遁故事累辭，乃授觀文殿學士、判福州、福建安撫大使，進封信國公，不拜；

translations.literal: In the fifth year, citing the precedent of Tu Yen's retirement and fleeing alone by cart at night, he repeatedly declined; he was then appointed Academician of the Kuan-wen Hall, judicial prefect of Fu-chou, Fukien Pacification Grand Commissioner, advanced and enfeoffed Duke of Hsin, and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, citing the precedent of Tu Yen, who retired and fled alone by cart at night, he repeatedly declined. He was then appointed academician of the Kuan-wen Hall, judicial prefect of Fu-chou, and Fukien pacification grand commissioner, and was enfeoffed as duke of Hsin, but he refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 充醴泉觀使，又不拜。

translations.literal: He was made Commissioner of the Li-ch'üan Abbey and again did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commissioner of the Li-ch'üan Abbey and again refused.

sentences.zh: 七年，再充醴泉使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he again served as commissioner of Li-ch'üan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he again served as commissioner of Li-ch'üan.

sentences.zh: 九年，授少傅、右丞相兼樞密使，引疾力辭，宰、掾、郎、曹遝至趣行，扶病至嵊縣，請辭不獲，乞還山林。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was appointed Junior Tutor, Right Chancellor concurrently Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; citing illness he forcefully declined; chancellors, clerks, bureau officers, and staff came in succession to urge departure; leaning on illness he reached Shêng County, requested dismissal but did not obtain it, and begged to return to the mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed junior tutor, right chancellor, and director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Citing illness, he forcefully declined, but chancellors, clerks, bureau officers, and staff came in succession to hurry him on his way. Supporting himself while ill, he reached Shêng County, asked to resign without success, and begged to return to the mountains and forests.

sentences.zh: 疏奏：「願上厲精寡欲，規當國者收人心，固邦本，勵將帥，飭州縣，重振恤。」

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "I wish Your Majesty to sharpen resolve and reduce desires; those governing the state should gather hearts, secure the state's foundation, encourage generals, rectify prefectures and counties, and vigorously renew compassionate care for the people."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote, "I pray that Your Majesty will sharpen your resolve and restrain your desires; those who govern the state should win back hearts, strengthen the foundation of the realm, encourage generals, discipline prefectures and counties, and vigorously restore care for the people."

sentences.zh: 扁舟徑歸。

translations.literal: He took a small boat and went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: He then took a small boat and went straight home.

sentences.zh: 使者以禍福告，夢鼎語之曰：「廉恥事大，死生事小，萬無可回之理。」

translations.literal: Envoys told him of fortune and calamity; Meng-ting said to them: "Integrity and shame are the greater matter, life and death the lesser; there is absolutely no reason to turn back."
translations.idiomatic: When envoys warned him of fortune and calamity, Meng-ting told them, "Honor and shame are the greater matter; life and death the lesser. There is absolutely no turning back."

sentences.zh: 似道大怒，台臣奏從歸田之請，詔仍少保、觀文殿大學士、醴泉觀使，不請祠祿。

translations.literal: Ssu-tao greatly angered; censorial officials memorialized to grant his request to return to his fields; an edict retained him as Junior Guardian, Grand Academician of the Kuan-wen Hall, and Commissioner of the Li-ch'üan Abbey, without requesting temple stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Ssu-tao was furious. Censorial officials memorialized to grant his request to retire to his fields, and an edict retained him as junior guardian, grand academician of the Kuan-wen Hall, and commissioner of the Li-ch'üan Abbey, without temple stipend.

sentences.zh: 瀛國公初即位，咨訪故老，夢鼎上封事，曰：「敦教道，訓廉德，厲臣節，拯民瘼，重士選，勸吏廉，懲吏奸，補軍籍。

translations.literal: When Duke Ying first ascended the throne, he consulted elderly statesmen; Meng-ting submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Promote the way of teaching, instruct in integrity, sharpen ministerial integrity, rescue the people's distress, value selection of scholars, encourage official integrity, punish official wickedness, and fill military registers.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Ying first ascended the throne and consulted elder statesmen, Meng-ting submitted a sealed memorial saying, "Promote the way of teaching, train officials in integrity, strengthen ministerial loyalty, relieve the people's distress, value the selection of scholars, encourage honest officials, punish corrupt ones, and fill the military registers.

sentences.zh: 授判慶元府、沿海制置大使，力辭，依前醴泉觀使兼侍讀，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed judicial prefect of Ch'ing-yüan and Coastal Pacification Grand Commissioner; he forcefully declined and, as before, served as Commissioner of the Li-ch'üan Abbey concurrently with Court Reader, and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial prefect of Ch'ing-yüan and coastal pacification grand commissioner, but forcefully declined and continued as commissioner of the Li-ch'üan Abbey with the added post of court reader, which he also refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 二年，益王即位於閩，召為少師、太乙宮使。

translations.literal: In the second year, Prince I acceded at Min and summoned him as Junior Preceptor and Commissioner of the T'ai-i Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Prince I acceded at Min, Meng-ting was summoned as junior preceptor and commissioner of the T'ai-i Palace.

sentences.zh: 航海遂行，道梗不能進，南向慟哭失聲而還。

translations.literal: He set out by sea voyage, but the route was blocked and he could not advance; he turned south, wept aloud without restraint, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He set out by sea, but the route was blocked and he could not proceed; facing south he wept aloud and turned back.

sentences.zh: 後二年卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 子應及，太府寺丞、知建德府軍器少監、駐戍軍馬；

translations.literal: His son Ying-chi served as Assistant Director of the Imperial Treasury, prefect of Chien-te, Vice Director of the Armory, and garrisoned army and horses;
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying-chi served as assistant director of the Imperial Treasury, prefect of Chien-te, vice director of the Armory, and commander of garrison troops and horses;

sentences.zh: 應有，朝請郎、太社令。

translations.literal: Ying-yu served as Gentleman for Court Audience and Director of the Altar of the God of the Soil.
translations.idiomatic: Ying-yu served as gentleman for court audience and director of the Altar of the God of the Soil.

sentences.zh: 馬廷鸞

translations.literal: Ma Tingluan
translations.idiomatic: Ma Tingluan

sentences.zh: 馬廷鸞，字翔仲，饒州樂平人。

translations.literal: Ma Tingluan, styled Hsiang-chung, was a native of Lo-p'ing in Jao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Tingluan, styled Hsiang-chung, was a native of Lo-p'ing in Jao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本灼之子，繼灼兄光後。

translations.literal: He was the born son of Chuo and succeeded after his elder brother Kuang of Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: He was Chuo's biological son and succeeded in the place of Chuo's elder brother Kuang.

sentences.zh: 甘貧力學，既冠，裏人聘為童子師，遇有酒食饌，則念母藜藿不給，為之食不下嚥。

translations.literal: Content with poverty, he studied diligently; after capping, villagers hired him as a children's teacher; when there were wine and food feastings, he thought of his mother's plain greens being insufficient and could not swallow food on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Poor but diligent in study, after reaching manhood he was hired by neighbors as a children's teacher. Whenever feasts were set before him, he thought of his mother eating plain greens at home and could not swallow the food.

sentences.zh: 登淳祐七年進士第，調池州教授，需次六年。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Ch'un-yu, was assigned as professor at Ch'ih Prefecture, and waited six years for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Ch'un-yu, was assigned as professor at Ch'ih Prefecture, and waited six years before taking up his post.

sentences.zh: 二年，進著作佐郎兼右司，遷將作少監。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was promoted to Assistant Compiler concurrently with the Right Bureau and transferred to Vice Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to assistant compiler with concurrent service in the Right Bureau, and was transferred to vice director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 三年，一再乞外補，不許。

translations.literal: In the third year, once and again he requested an external appointment and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he repeatedly asked for an outside appointment, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 廷鸞論貢舉三事：嚴鄉里之舉，重台省之覆試，訪山林之遺逸。

translations.literal: T'ing-luan discussed three matters of the examinations: tighten village recommendations, weight the provincial re-examination, and seek recluses in mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: T'ing-luan proposed three reforms to the examination system: tighten local recommendations, give greater weight to re-examination by the provincial offices, and seek out recluses in the mountains and forests.

sentences.zh: 又言荒政，宜蠲除被災州縣租賦之不可得者。

translations.literal: He also spoke on famine policy, saying that rent and levies from disaster-affected prefectures and counties that could not be collected should be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke on famine relief, arguing that rent and levies owed by disaster-stricken prefectures and counties but impossible to collect should be remitted.

sentences.zh: 擢軍器監兼左司，兼太子右諭德，升左諭德，行國子司業，乞免兼左司。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Armory concurrently with the Left Bureau, concurrently Right Mentor to the Crown Prince, promoted to Left Mentor, acting Vice Director of the Imperial Academy, and requested exemption from concurrent service in the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Armory with concurrent service in the Left Bureau, then also made right mentor to the crown prince, promoted to left mentor, and acting vice director of the Imperial Academy; he asked to be relieved of his concurrent post in the Left Bureau.

sentences.zh: 輪對，言：「集和平之福者自陛下之身始，養和平之德者自陛下之心始。」

translations.literal: In audience rotation he said: "He who gathers the blessings of peace begins with Your Majesty's person; he who nurtures the virtue of peace begins with Your Majesty's mind."
translations.idiomatic: In audience rotation he said, "The blessings of peace must begin with Your Majesty's own conduct; the virtue of peace must begin in Your Majesty's own heart."

sentences.zh: 兼翰林權直，擢秘書少監，升權直學士院。

translations.literal: Concurrently Acting Duty Officer of the Han-lin Academy, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and then to Acting Academician of the Academy Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrently acting duty officer of the Han-lin Academy, he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and then to acting academician of the Academy Institute.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢起居舍人兼太子右庶子兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was promoted to Attendance Drafter concurrently with Right Subordinate to the Crown Prince, concurrently Compiler of the National History Academy and Examiner of the Veritable Records Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to attendance drafter, concurrently right subordinate to the crown prince, compiler of the National History Academy, and examiner of the Veritable Records Academy.

sentences.zh: 入奏言：「太史必當謹書災異。

translations.literal: Entering to memorialize, he said: "The grand astrologer must carefully record anomalies and disasters.
translations.idiomatic: In memorial to the throne he said, "The grand astrologer must carefully record anomalies and disasters.

sentences.zh: 願陛下翕受敷施，以壯人才之精神；

translations.literal: May Your Majesty harmoniously receive and extend benefits, to strengthen the spirit of talented men;
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty harmoniously receive Heaven's warnings and extend benefits, so as to strengthen the spirit of talented men;

sentences.zh: 虛心容納，以植人言之骨幹。

translations.literal: with an open mind receive and accept, to plant the backbone of public speech.
translations.idiomatic: and with an open mind receive remonstrance, so as to strengthen the backbone of public speech.

sentences.zh: 念邦本而以公滅私，嚴邊備而思患豫防。」

translations.literal: Think on the foundation of the state and extinguish selfishness with public-mindedness; strengthen frontier defense and think ahead to prepare against troubles."
translations.idiomatic: Keep the foundation of the state in mind and subordinate private interest to the public good; strengthen frontier defenses and prepare against trouble before it arises."

sentences.zh: 時再召用宋臣，廷鸞引何郯之說進，極言宋臣不可用，帝從之。

translations.literal: At the time Sung Ch'en was again summoned for employment; T'ing-luan cited Ho T'an's argument in memorial and spoke at length that Sung Ch'en could not be used; the emperor followed him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sung Ch'en was again being considered for office; T'ing-luan cited Ho T'an's argument and strongly urged that Sung Ch'en must not be employed, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 薦士二十人，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He recommended twenty scholars and was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended twenty scholars and was promoted to secretariat drafting officer.

sentences.zh: 程奎污穢詭秘，不當補將仕郎；

translations.literal: Ch'eng K'uei was filthy and crafty in secrecy and ought not be supplemented as General Attendant Gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: Ch'eng K'uei was corrupt and deceitful and ought not be granted appointment as general attendant gentleman;

sentences.zh: 王之淵為大全黨，不當通判江州；

translations.literal: Wang Chih-yüan was of Ta-ch'üan's faction and ought not be deputy prefect of Kiang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chih-yüan belonged to Ta-ch'üan's faction and ought not be made deputy prefect of Kiang Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 朱熠不當知慶元府及為制置使；

translations.literal: Chu I ought not govern Ch'ing-yüan Prefecture and serve as pacification commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Chu I ought not be made prefect of Ch'ing-yüan and pacification commissioner;

sentences.zh: 林奭、趙必、張稱孫不當與郡：皆繳還詞頭。

translations.literal: Lin Shuang, Chao Pi, and Chang Ch'eng-sun ought not receive prefectures: all appointment documents were returned.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shuang, Chao Pi, and Chang Ch'eng-sun were unfit for prefectural posts: he returned all their appointment documents.

sentences.zh: 兼國史實錄院。

translations.literal: He concurrently served in the National History and Veritable Records Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently in the National History and Veritable Records Academy.

sentences.zh: 五年，彗出，上疏極言天人之際。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when a comet appeared, he submitted a memorial speaking at length on the interface of Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when a comet appeared, he submitted a memorial speaking at length on the relationship between Heaven and human affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 理宗遺詔、度宗登極詔，皆廷鸞所草。

translations.literal: Emperor Li-tsung's death edict and Emperor Tu-tsung's accession edict were both drafted by T'ing-luan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Li-tsung's death edict and Emperor Tu-tsung's accession edict were both drafted by T'ing-luan.

sentences.zh: 兼侍讀，辭，不許。

translations.literal: Concurrently Court Reader, he declined and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed concurrently as court reader, he declined but was not permitted to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 疏列孝宗之政以告。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial enumerating Hsiao-tsung's policies to inform the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial setting forth the policies of Emperor Hsiao-tsung for the throne's guidance.

sentences.zh: 升直學士院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Academy Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Academy Institute.

sentences.zh: 咸淳元年，進端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事兼同提舉編修《經武要略》。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hsien-ch'un, he was promoted to Academician of the Tuan-ming Hall, Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and concurrently Co-Director of the compilation of the Essential Military Compendium.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hsien-ch'un he was promoted to academician of the Tuan-ming Hall and signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, while also serving as co-director of the compilation of the Essential Military Compendium.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 三年，同知樞密院事兼同提舉編修《經武要略》。

translations.literal: In the third year, he served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs concurrently with Co-Director of the compilation of the Essential Military Compendium.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and co-director of the compilation of the Essential Military Compendium.

sentences.zh: 入奏言培命脈，植根本，崇寬大，行仁厚。

translations.literal: Entering to memorialize, he spoke on nurturing the life-vessels, planting the roots, honoring magnanimity, and practicing benevolence and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: In memorial to the throne he spoke of nurturing the life-vessels of the state, planting deep roots, honoring magnanimity, and practicing benevolence.

sentences.zh: 又言：「恢大度以優容，虛聖心而延佇，推內恕以假借，忍難行而聽納，則情無不達，理無不盡，奸人破膽，直士吐氣，天下事尚可為也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Restore broad-mindedness for forbearance, empty the sacred heart to wait patiently, extend inner forgiveness to lend trust, endure what is hard to practice and listen and accept—then feeling will nowhere fail to reach, principle nowhere fail to exhaust, villains will lose courage, upright men will breathe freely, and affairs under Heaven may still be accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "If Your Majesty restores broad-minded forbearance, keeps an open heart and waits patiently, extends inner forgiveness and tolerates what is hard to bear, then no feeling will go unheeded, no principle unexamined, villains will lose heart, upright men will speak freely, and affairs under Heaven may still be set right."

sentences.zh: 兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: Concurrently Acting Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently appointed acting grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 五年，進參知政事兼同知樞密院事，進右丞相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to Grand Councilor concurrently with Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and then promoted to Right Chancellor concurrently Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to grand councilor and vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and then to right chancellor and director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 八年，九疏乞罷政。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he submitted nine memorials begging to resign from government.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he submitted nine memorials asking to leave office.

sentences.zh: 九年，依舊觀文殿大學士、知紹興府、浙東安撫大使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he retained his former posts as Guanwen Hall Grand Academician, Prefect of Shaoxing, and Grand Pacification Commissioner of Eastern Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he retained his posts as Guanwen Hall grand academician, prefect of Shaoxing, and grand pacification commissioner of eastern Zhe.

sentences.zh: 上疏辭免，依舊職提舉臨安府洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He memorialized declining the appointment and was made Intendant of Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an Prefecture, retaining his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: He declined by memorial and was appointed intendant of Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an, keeping his former rank.

sentences.zh: 度宗初年，詔詢故老，專以修攘大計叩之趙葵。

translations.literal: In the early years of Duzong, an edict inquired of old ministers; the great plan of defense and recovery was directed specifically to Zhao Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duzong's reign the court consulted elder statesmen; on the grand strategy of defense and recovery it turned specifically to Zhao Kui.

sentences.zh: 葵極意指陳曰：「老臣出入兵間，備諳此事，願朝廷謹之重之。」

translations.literal: Kui pointed emphatically and stated: "This old minister has gone in and out among armies and is thoroughly versed in these matters; I hope the court will treat them with care and weight."
translations.idiomatic: Kui pointed emphatically and said, "This old servant has spent his life in the armies and knows these matters well; I beg the court to treat them with the utmost care."

sentences.zh: 似道作色曰：「此三京敗事者，詞臣失言。」

translations.literal: Jia Sidao changed color and said, "This is the man who ruined the Three Capitals—a drafting official who misspoke."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao's face darkened and he said, "This is the man who lost the Three Capitals—a drafting official who has spoken out of turn."

sentences.zh: 廷鸞每見文法密，功賞稽遲，將校不出死力，于邊閫升辟，稍越拘攣。

translations.literal: Tingluan, whenever he saw regulations too strict, rewards and merit grants delayed, and officers and soldiers unwilling to exert themselves to the death, would in border commands promote and appoint men, slightly exceeding the usual constraints.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tingluan saw regulations too rigid, rewards delayed, and commanders holding back, he would promote men in the border commands, bending the rules a little.

sentences.zh: 似道頗疑異己，黥堂吏以泄其憤。

translations.literal: Sidao was quite suspicious of those unlike himself and had a hall clerk tattooed as punishment to vent his anger.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao grew suspicious of rivals and had a clerk in his hall branded with ink to vent his anger.

sentences.zh: 及辭相位，帝惻怛久之曰：「丞相勉為朕留。」

translations.literal: When he resigned the chief ministership, the emperor was long moved with compassion and said, "Chief Councillor, do your best to remain for Us."
translations.idiomatic: When he resigned as chief councillor, the emperor was moved for a long while and said, "Chief Councillor, please stay on for my sake."

sentences.zh: 廷鸞言：「臣死亡無日，恐不得再見君父。

translations.literal: Tingluan said, "Your subject's death is not far off; I fear I may not again see my sovereign father.
translations.idiomatic: Tingluan said, "I have not long to live and fear I may never see Your Majesty again.

sentences.zh: 然國事方殷，疆圉孔棘。

translations.literal: Yet state affairs are pressing and the frontier is critically perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Yet state affairs are urgent and the frontier is in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 天下安危，人主不知；

translations.literal: the safety or danger of all under Heaven—the sovereign does not know;
translations.idiomatic: Whether the realm is safe or in peril, the sovereign does not know;

sentences.zh: 國家利害，群臣不知；

translations.literal: the benefit or harm to the state—the ministers do not know;
translations.idiomatic: what helps or harms the state—the ministers do not know;

sentences.zh: 軍前勝負，列閫不知。

translations.literal: victory or defeat before the armies—the commanders in the field do not know.
translations.idiomatic: victory or defeat on the battlefield—even the frontier commanders do not know.

sentences.zh: 陛下與元老大臣惟懷永圖，臣死且瞑目。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty and the elder ministers will only cherish a long-term design, your subject may die with eyes closed."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty and the elder ministers will only plan for the long term, I can die in peace."

sentences.zh: 頓首涕泣而退。

translations.literal: He bowed his head to the ground, weeping, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed, weeping, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 瀛國公即位，召不至。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Yingguo ascended the throne, he was summoned but did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Yingguo ascended the throne, he was summoned but did not come.

sentences.zh: 自罷相歸，又十七年而薨。

translations.literal: After he was dismissed as chancellor and returned home, another seventeen years passed before he died.
translations.idiomatic: After he left the chancellorship and returned home, another seventeen years passed before he died.

sentences.zh: 所著《六經集傳》、《語孟會編》、《楚辭補記》、《洙泗裔編》、《讀莊筆記》、《張氏祝氏皇極觀物外篇》諸書。

translations.literal: Among the works he authored were 《六經集傳》, 《語孟會編》, 《楚辭補記》, 《洙泗裔編》, 《讀莊筆記》, 《張氏祝氏皇極觀物外篇》, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included 《六經集傳》, 《語孟會編》, 《楚辭補記》, 《洙泗裔編》, 《讀莊筆記》, 《張氏祝氏皇極觀物外篇》, and other works.

sentences.zh: 論曰：史彌遠廢親立疏，諱聞直言。

translations.literal: The judgment states: Shi Miyuan deposed the close heir and established the distant one, and shunned hearing straight speech.
translations.idiomatic: The historians' judgment: Shi Miyuan deposed the heir in favor of a distant prince and refused to hear honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 鄭清之墮名於再相之日。

translations.literal: Zheng Qingzhi's reputation fell on the day he became chief councillor a second time.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qingzhi's reputation suffered when he took the chief ministership a second time.

sentences.zh: 彌遠之罪既著，故當時不樂嵩之之繼也，因喪起復，群起攻之，然固將才也。

translations.literal: Miyuan's crimes being already manifest, men of the time were displeased that Songzhi should succeed him; because he was recalled from mourning to resume office, they rose up to attack him—yet he was indeed a man of military talent.
translations.idiomatic: With Miyuan's crimes well known, the court was unhappy that Songzhi should follow him; recalled from mourning, he was attacked from all sides—yet he was genuinely a capable general.

sentences.zh: 董槐毋得而議之矣。

translations.literal: As for Dong Huai, there is nothing left to debate.
translations.idiomatic: Of Dong Huai there is little left to dispute.

sentences.zh: 葉夢鼎、馬廷鸞之所遭逢，其不幸也夫！

translations.literal: What Ye Mengding and Ma Tingluan encountered—how unfortunate!
translations.idiomatic: What befell Ye Mengding and Ma Tingluan—how bitter their fate!
